definition_zh: 哨子；口哨；哨声；吹口哨；鸣笛
definition_en: a small tube of metal or plastic blown to make a sharp sound, and the sound or the act of blowing through pursed lips
core_image: 裁判把银色小哨子含在嘴里，腮帮子一鼓，一声长响划过球场
scene: 球赛最后几秒，裁判把哨子举到嘴边用力吹了一下，全场忽然安静下来。The referee blew the whistle and pointed at the penalty spot.
sceneCN: 这里 whistle 是「哨子」（第 1 个义项：用嘴吹出尖锐声音的小管）；句意为裁判吹响哨子并指向点球点。银色小哨与划破空气的一声长响，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The small blowing instrument
senses.definition: a small device, often metal or plastic, that makes a loud high sound when air is forced through it
senses.definitionCN: 一种小巧的器具，多为金属或塑料制成，用力吹气时发出响亮的高音
senses.example: The referee blew the whistle and pointed at the penalty spot.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判吹响哨子，指向点球点。
senses.why: The instrument is named by the sound it makes, so the object and its noise share one word.
senses.whyCN: 这个器具是以它发出的声音命名的，所以器具与声音共用一个词。

senses.title: The sound made by lips
senses.definition: the clear musical sound produced by forcing breath through a small round opening of the lips
senses.definitionCN: 把嘴唇收成小圆口、用力呼气而发出的清亮乐音
senses.example: A long whistle came from the boy on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 墙头上的男孩打了一声长长的口哨。
senses.why: Whistling with the lips needs no tool, yet it copies the same pipe of the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 用嘴唇吹口哨不需要任何工具，但它模仿的正是哨子那根小管。

senses.title: To make a whistling sound
senses.definition: to make a high sound by blowing through the lips or through an instrument, often to call or warn
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴唇或乐器发出高音，常用来呼叫或示警
senses.example: He whistled to his dog across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他在田野那头对着狗吹了一声口哨。
senses.why: The verb simply puts the sound into action, whether through lips, a train funnel or a kettle.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词只是把声音变成动作，无论发声的是嘴唇、火车汽笛还是水壶。

senses.title: To move with a rushing sound
senses.definition: to travel very fast with a sound like wind forced through a narrow gap
senses.definitionCN: 快速移动，并发出像风挤过窄缝一样的声音
senses.example: A bullet whistled past his ear and buried itself in the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗子弹呼啸着擦过他的耳朵，钻进树里。
senses.why: Fast air through a thin gap makes exactly the pipe sound, so the word spread to anything rushing by.
senses.whyCN: 快速的气流穿过细缝时，发出的正是哨管般的声音，于是这个词扩展到一切疾驰而过之物。

senses.title: To reveal a secret to the police
senses.definition: in the phrase blow the whistle, to report wrongdoing inside an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在 blow the whistle 这一说法中，指揭发机构内部的违法行为
senses.example: She was the first to whistle on the fake receipts.
senses.exampleCN: 她是第一个举报假发票的人。
senses.why: A referee stops the game with a whistle, and a reporter stops a crime the same way in this image.
senses.whyCN: 裁判用哨声叫停比赛，而举报者用同样的画面叫停一桩罪行。

intro.en: Whistle is an imitative word: Old English hwistle named both the pipe and the sound, likely copying the hiss of air through a narrow hole.
intro.cn: whistle 是拟声词：古英语 hwistle 同时指那根哨管和它发出的声音，很可能是模仿气流穿过窄孔时的嘶声。

items.en: hwistle was the noun for a pipe or flute, and the verb hwistlian meant to make that sound.
items.cn: hwistle 指哨管或笛子，动词 hwistlian 表示发出这种声音。

items.en: The initial h was pronounced before the w, as in many old English words of that shape.
items.cn: 这个词开头的 h 在 w 之前发音，许多这一形状的古英语词都如此。

items.en: The h fell silent and the spelling moved towards whistle, while the meaning widened to lips and to birds.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 h 不再发音，拼写移向 whistle，词义也扩展到用嘴唇与鸟类。

items.en: Steam engines and kettles added the sense of a mechanical warning, and trains whistled at crossings.
items.cn: 蒸汽机与水壶带来了机械警示之义，火车在道口鸣笛。

items.en: Since the late twentieth century to blow the whistle has meant to expose wrongdoing inside an organization.
items.cn: 二十世纪末以来，blow the whistle 被用来表示揭发机构内部的违法行为。

note.en: The first group gathers other small wind instruments and their sounds, the second the acts of calling out or revealing something.
note.cn: 第一组收其他吹奏小乐器及其声音，第二组收呼喊与揭发一类动作。

entries.definition: A long thin pipe held sideways and played with the fingers.
A hollow instrument sounded by breath, louder and lower.
A loud device on a vehicle that wails as a warning.
A tube you blow into, the physical body of a whistle.
To make a long hollow call, as an owl or a horn does.
To give a sign that something should start or stop.
To bring a hidden wrong into the open, as a whistle-blower does.

normalIntro.en: Whistle is a sound word, so it is best fixed by hearing one rather than by staring at the letters.
normalIntro.cn: whistle 是个声音词，记住它最好的办法是听一声，而不是盯着字母看。

normal.en: The letters w h i s p e r are close to whisper, a sound made with almost no voice.
normal.cn: whistle 与 whisper 长得很像，后者是用几乎不带嗓音的口型发出的声音。

normal.en: A whistle is a pipe you blow, so picture a tiny tube rather than a person.
normal.cn: 哨子是你吹的那根小管，所以要想一根小管，而不是一个人。

normal.en: The referee, the kettle, the train and the bird all use the same sharp note.
normal.cn: 裁判、水壶、火车和鸟，用的是同一个尖锐的音。

normal.en: To blow the whistle is to stop the play of a dishonest office.
normal.cn: blow the whistle 就是叫停一间不诚实办公室里的那场比赛。

normal.en: The -le ending makes a light ending note, just as the sound dies away.
normal.cn: 词尾的 -le 像一声轻巧的收尾，正如声音渐渐散去。

abstract.en: Hear a flat high note cutting the noise of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 听见一个平直的高音切开人群的嘈杂。

abstract.en: Feel the small round hole of the lips holding the air back.
abstract.cn: 感觉嘴唇的小圆口把气暂时憋住。

abstract.en: Watch a dog turn its head before the sound has ended.
abstract.cn: 看那只狗在声音还没停时就已经转过头。

examples.en: The referee blew his whistle and the game restarted.
examples.cn: 裁判吹响哨子，比赛重新开始。

examples.en: She whistled softly while washing the dishes.
examples.cn: 她一边洗碗一边轻轻吹口哨。

examples.en: The wind whistled through the broken window all night.
examples.cn: 整夜风都从破窗里呼呼地响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威哨」——威力十足的哨子，一吹整条街都听见。

root: 拟声词：古英语 hwistle（哨管、笛，兼指其声）→ 中古英语 whistle → 现代英语 whistle；同族有 whistler、whistle-blower。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as the little pipe and its sound, widens from lips to machines, slides into the rushing sound of fast movement, and finally becomes the image of exposing a secret.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从哨管与哨声出发，由嘴唇扩展到机械，再滑向疾驰而过的呼啸声，最后成为揭发秘密的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver pipe held between two lips, one long high note.
core.cn: 核心意象：两片嘴唇之间的一支银色小管，一声高而长的音。

branches.en: The object branch: the referee points at the penalty spot.
branches.cn: 器物分支：裁判指向点球点。

branches.en: The sound branch: a long call from the boy on the wall.
branches.cn: 声音分支：墙头男孩发出的一声长哨。

branches.en: The action branch: whistling a dog home across a field.
branches.cn: 动作分支：在田野那头用口哨唤狗回家。

branches.en: The rushing branch: a bullet passing the ear.
branches.cn: 呼啸分支：一颗子弹擦过耳边。

branches.en: The exposing branch: stopping the play with a report.
branches.cn: 揭发分支：用一纸举报叫停比赛。

intro.en: Whistle is an imitation of sound rather than a built form, yet it takes the usual verb endings and appears inside compounds such as whistle-blower.
intro.cn: whistle 是声音的模仿而非构造成分，但它能带普通动词词尾，并出现在 whistle-blower 这类复合词中。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and imitative, so it has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below belong to borrowed relatives only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语的拟声词，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目只是借入的相关词。

items.example: It is the plain base form.
items.exampleCN: 它就是朴素的词根形式。

items.example: It makes the word sound like a small flute.
items.exampleCN: 它让这个词听起来像一支小笛子。

items.meaning: a person who reports a wrong
items.example: The compound keeps the referee image.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词保留了裁判的形象。

items.meaning: a small station where a train waits briefly
items.example: The train sound names the halt itself.
items.exampleCN: 火车声给这个停靠点命了名。

items.meaning: a silent call for dogs, or a coded hint
items.meaningCN: 唤狗的无形哨；隐语暗号
items.example: The image moved from dogs to politics.
items.exampleCN: 这个形象从狗延伸到了政治。

latinEntries.example: Its hiss is the same narrow-air sound.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它嘶嘶的气流声正是同一种窄缝声。

definition_zh: 白色；白色的；白人的；苍白；空白
definition_en: the colour of fresh snow or of milk, and anything of that colour, pale, or left blank
core_image: 院子里刚落下的一层雪，白得反光，连屋顶的边都看不清
scene: 清晨推门，院子里的雪一夜未动，白得刺眼，脚印一踩就留下深灰的坑。After the storm the hills were white as far as the eye could see.
sceneCN: 这里 white 是「白色」（第 1 个义项：雪或牛奶那样的颜色）；句意为风暴过后，目力所及的山全是白色。那层反光的、连屋顶边缘都看不清的雪，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The colour of snow
senses.definition: the lightest colour, the one that reflects almost all the light reaching it, like fresh snow or milk
senses.definitionCN: 最浅的颜色，几乎反射所有照来的光，如新雪或牛奶
senses.example: After the storm the hills were white as far as the eye could see.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，目力所及的山全是白色。
senses.why: It is the colour with nothing added, the visual point where every other colour is absent.
senses.whyCN: 这是什么也不加的颜色，是其他颜色都不在场时的那一点。

senses.title: Very pale in the face
senses.definition: used of a face that has lost its natural colour through fear, illness or cold
senses.definitionCN: 形容脸色因恐惧、疾病或寒冷而失去血色
senses.example: She went white when the doctor read the result.
senses.exampleCN: 医生念出结果时，她的脸刷地白了。
senses.why: Blood leaving the skin leaves the same colour as snow behind, so the word doubles as a sign of shock.
senses.whyCN: 血液离开皮肤时留下的正是雪那样的颜色，于是这个词也成了惊吓的记号。

senses.title: A blank part
senses.definition: a space left empty on a printed page or a form, waiting to be filled
senses.definitionCN: 印刷页或表格上留出、等待填写的一块空地
senses.example: Write your answers in the white space below each question.
senses.exampleCN: 把答案写在每道题下面的空白处。
senses.why: An unprinted sheet is simply paper showing through, and paper at that time was white.
senses.whyCN: 未印字的纸页就是纸本身的颜色透出来，而当时的纸正是白的。

senses.title: The transparent part of an egg
senses.definition: the clear liquid around the yolk of an egg, which turns white when cooked
senses.definitionCN: 蛋中央蛋黄周围的透明液体，煮熟后变成白色
senses.example: Beat the whites of three eggs until they stand in soft peaks.
senses.exampleCN: 把三个蛋的蛋白打到能立起柔软的尖角。
senses.why: Raw it looks clear, cooked it turns white, so English named it for the state you see on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 生时透明，熟后变白，于是英语按盘中看到的样子给它命名。

senses.title: A group of people and their history
senses.definition: used of people with light skin, or of the social category built around them
senses.definitionCN: 指肤色浅的人，或围绕他们形成的社会类别
senses.example: The law treated white and black families very differently then.
senses.exampleCN: 那时法律对白人家庭和黑人家庭的处理大不相同。
senses.why: A colour word was placed on skin, and the label hardened into a social fact that has to be read with care.
senses.whyCN: 一个颜色词被贴到皮肤上，这个标签又固化成社会事实，使用时须格外谨慎。

intro.en: White comes from Old English hwit, which goes back to a Germanic root meaning bright or shining, not primarily a colour.
intro.cn: white 源自古英语 hwit，可上溯到表示「明亮、发亮」的日耳曼语词根，最初并不主要是颜色。

items.en: The old root meant bright and shining, the way light looks when it hits a smooth surface.
items.cn: 古老的词根表示明亮、发亮，即光打在光滑表面上呈现的样子。

items.en: Hwit described snow, milk, silver and hair, and also carried the sense of being pure or fortunate.
items.cn: hwit 描述雪、牛奶、银和白发，同时带有纯洁或幸运之意。

items.en: The spelling shifted to whit, whyt and finally white, while the h stayed silent after w.
items.cn: 拼写先后变为 whit、whyt，最后成为 white，而 w 之后的 h 始终不发音。

items.en: The word spread to faces, to eggs, to empty page space and to the colour of coffee with milk.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到脸色、蛋、书页空白以及加奶咖啡的颜色。

items.en: From the nineteenth century it was applied to skin and to whole populations, a use that carries a heavy social history.
items.cn: 自十九世纪起，它被用于肤色与整个族群，这一用法背负沉重的社会历史。

note.en: The first group gathers other colours that sit beside white, the second the words for paleness and for plainness.
note.cn: 第一组收与白色相邻的其他颜色，第二组收表示苍白与素净的说法。

entries.definition: The colour of coal, the darkest end of the scale.
The colour between black and white, like stone or cloud.
Light in colour, close to white but weaker.
The white stuff itself, a common way to picture white.
Left empty, with nothing written on it.
The quality of being clean and unmixed.
A soft white stone used for writing.

normalIntro.en: White is a colour word with a shining origin, so it should be remembered with light rather than with paint.
normalIntro.cn: white 是带有「发亮」出处的颜色词，因此要借光线而不是颜料来记。

normal.en: The whole word runs light to dark: white, grey, black, like a staircase of shade.
normal.cn: 整个词处在由浅到深的顺序里：white、grey、black，像一级级明暗台阶。

normal.en: A sheet of snow reflects almost everything, which is why it looks white.
normal.cn: 一层雪几乎反射所有东西，所以看起来是白的。

normal.en: A face goes white when blood leaves it, the same colour, a worse reason.
normal.cn: 血液离开脸部时脸会变白，颜色相同，原因却更糟。

normal.en: The white of an egg turns white only when cooked.
normal.cn: 蛋的蛋白只有煮熟后才变白。

normal.en: White space on a page is the printer leaving the paper alone.
normal.cn: 页面的空白就是印刷工让纸保持不变。

abstract.en: Feel the glare of snow on a bright morning.
abstract.cn: 感觉清晨雪面上的那一层反光。

abstract.en: Hear the silence of a white field with no birds.
abstract.cn: 听那片没有鸟的白野里的寂静。

abstract.en: See a hand held up in front of a window, bloodless.
abstract.cn: 看见一只手挡在窗前，没有血色。

examples.en: The cat has one white paw and three black ones.
examples.cn: 这只猫一只爪子是白的，另外三只是黑的。

examples.en: His face turned white with anger.
examples.cn: 他气得脸色发白。

examples.en: I take my coffee white, with plenty of milk.
examples.cn: 我喝咖啡要加奶，加很多奶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪特」——雪白得歪着头看，太刺眼了。

root: 日耳曼语词根（明亮、发亮）→ 古英语 hwit（白）→ 中古英语 white → 现代英语 white；同族有 whiten、whiteness、whitewash。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the shining colour of snow, then slips onto faces, onto blank paper, onto eggs, and finally onto skin and social groups.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从雪那样发亮的颜色出发，再滑到脸上、空白的纸上、蛋上，最后落到皮肤与人群分类上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field of untouched snow throwing the light back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片无人踩过的雪，把光原样抛回。

branches.en: The colour branch: hills white as far as the eye can see.
branches.cn: 颜色分支：目力所及的白色山峦。

branches.en: The fear branch: a face going white at a result.
branches.cn: 惊吓分支：听到结果时发白的脸。

branches.en: The page branch: answers written in the white space.
branches.cn: 页面分支：写在空白处的答案。

branches.en: The kitchen branch: egg whites beaten into peaks.
branches.cn: 厨房分支：打成尖角的蛋白。

branches.en: The social branch: a colour label put on people.
branches.cn: 社会分支：贴在人群身上的颜色标签。

intro.en: White is a free word that adds the suffixes -ness, -en and -ish, and it forms compounds freely, as in whitewash and whiteboard.
intro.cn: white 是自由使用的词，可加 -ness、-en、-ish 等后缀，也能自由构成 whitewash、whiteboard 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The native word has no Latin source; the Latin entries below show the borrowed relatives such as albus and candidus used in technical names.
latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目展示 albus、candidus 一类借入的相关词，它们多用于术语。

items.example: It works as noun, adjective and verb.
items.exampleCN: 它可作名词、形容词与动词。

items.meaning: to cover with a pale coat
items.example: It gives whitewash, covering walls or facts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 whitewash，指刷墙或掩盖事实。

items.example: It builds names such as whitefish.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 whitefish 一类名称。

items.example: It never takes a plural form.
items.exampleCN: 这一说法不用复数形式。

latinEntries.example: It survives in album, originally a blank tablet.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它保存在 album 中，原意是空白的木板。

latinEntries.example: It gives candid, frank as a white surface.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出 candid，像白色表面一样坦率。

definition_zh: 谁；何人；（关系代词）…的人
definition_en: the question word for a person, and the relative word that introduces a clause about a person
core_image: 一群人站在门口，目光齐刷刷地转向门边，问的只是那一个人是谁
scene: 有人敲门，屋里的人抬起头互相看了看，谁都想知道门外站着的是谁。Who is knocking at the door at this hour?
sceneCN: 这里 who 是「谁」（第 1 个义项：询问人的疑问词）；句意为这个时间是谁在敲门。一群人目光齐刷刷转向门口的那一幕，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Asking which person
senses.definition: used at the start of a question to ask which person is meant
senses.definitionCN: 放在问句开头，询问指的是哪个人
senses.example: Who is knocking at the door at this hour?
senses.exampleCN: 这个时间是谁在敲门？
senses.why: The word asks for a person only, which is why it cannot be used for a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只询问人，所以不能用来问物。

senses.title: A relative word for a person
senses.definition: used after a noun to add a clause about that person
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词之后，为该名词补充一个从句
senses.example: The woman who lives above us is a nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 住在我们楼上的那个女人是护士。
senses.why: The same word slides from asking to linking, joining two sentences about one person.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从发问滑向连接，把关于同一个人的两句话连起来。

senses.title: In a noun clause
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that acts as the subject or object of a bigger sentence
senses.definitionCN: 引导一个充当更大句子主语或宾语的从句
senses.example: I do not know who sent the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 我不知道那封信是谁寄的。
senses.why: Here the question is folded inside a statement, and the word keeps its asking shape.
senses.whyCN: 这里疑问被折进了一句陈述里，而这个词仍保持发问的形状。

senses.title: Who as a fixed opening
senses.definition: in set phrases such as who knows, or in titles and headings
senses.definitionCN: 用于 who knows 等固定说法，或用于标题
senses.example: Who knows, the bus may still be waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 谁知道呢，也许那趟车还在等。
senses.why: Short questions became idioms, and the word froze inside them.
senses.whyCN: 短问句变成了习语，这个词也就冻结在其中。

intro.en: Who descends from Old English hwa, the interrogative stem for persons, from the same Germanic root as what and why.
intro.cn: who 源自古英语 hwa，指人的疑问词干，与 what、why 同出一个日耳曼语词根。

items.en: One old root supplied the whole family of question words, each with a different ending for person, thing or reason.
items.cn: 一个古老词根供给了整个疑问词家族，各自的词尾区分人、物与原因。

items.en: Hwa was the nominative form, hwaene the accusative and hwaes the genitive.
items.cn: hwa 是主格，hwaene 是宾格，hwaes 是所有格。

items.en: English simplified the endings to who, whom and whose, and the spelling fixed around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语把词尾简化为 who、whom、whose，拼写在十四世纪前后固定下来。

items.en: Who took over the relative work from older that and which when a person was meant.
items.cn: 当所指为人时，who 接替了 older that 与 which 的关系代词功能。

items.en: Spoken English increasingly uses who in object position, while careful writing keeps whom.
items.cn: 口语中 who 越来越多地出现在宾语位置，而严谨的书面语仍保留 whom。

note.en: The first group gathers the other question words of the same shape, the second the words that link clauses about people or things.
note.cn: 第一组收同一形状的其他疑问词，第二组收连接人与物从句的词。

entries.definition: The object form, used after a preposition.
The possessive form, asking about ownership.
The question word for things, not people.
The question word for place.
A relative word for things or a chosen one of a set.
A plain relative word that can refer to people or things.
An unnamed person, the answer who often looks for.

normalIntro.en: Who is one of the shortest question words, so it should be attached to a gesture of pointing at a person.
normalIntro.cn: who 是最短的疑问词之一，最好把它和「指向某个人」的手势绑在一起。

normal.en: Who has an o, like an open mouth waiting for a name.
normal.cn: who 里有个 o，像一张张开等名字的嘴。

normal.en: Ask who for people, and what for seats, and the pair stays clean.
normal.cn: 问人用 who，问位置用 what，两者就不会混。

normal.en: Who knows is a shrug in two words.
normal.cn: who knows 用两个词就是一个耸肩。

normal.en: The man who called: who ties the noun to its story.
normal.cn: the man who called 中，who 把名词和它的故事系在一起。

normal.en: Whom is the old shadow of who, still seen after prepositions.
normal.cn: whom 是 who 的旧日影子，仍见于介词之后。

abstract.en: Feel a whole room turning towards a door.
abstract.cn: 感觉一屋子人齐刷刷转向门口。

abstract.en: Hear a name being waited for in silence.
abstract.cn: 听一段等着被名字填满的沉默。

abstract.en: See a single finger raised at a crowd.
abstract.cn: 看见一根手指从人群中举起。

examples.en: Who told you about the party?
examples.cn: 谁告诉你聚会的事？

examples.en: The doctor who treated me was very patient.
examples.cn: 给我治病的那位医生非常耐心。

examples.en: She asked who would like more tea.
examples.cn: 她问还有谁想再来点茶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呼」——一推门就呼一声：是谁在那儿？

root: 日耳曼语疑问词根 → 古英语 hwa（主格）→ 中古英语 who → 现代英语 who；同族有 whom、whose、whoever。

sensesIntro.en: The word asks which person, then turns into a link after a noun, then introduces a clause inside a sentence, and finally freezes in short phrases.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先问是哪个人，接着在名词后变成连接词，再引导句子内的从句，最后冻在短句里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room turning towards one door, waiting for a name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一屋子人转向同一扇门，等一个名字。

branches.en: The asking branch: who is knocking at this hour.
branches.cn: 发问分支：这个时间是谁在敲门。

branches.en: The linking branch: the woman who lives above us.
branches.cn: 连接分支：住在楼上的那个女人。

branches.en: The clause branch: I do not know who sent it.
branches.cn: 从句分支：我不知道是谁寄的。

branches.en: The idiom branch: who knows, the bus may wait.
branches.cn: 习语分支：谁知道呢，车也许还在等。

branches.en: The pointing branch: one finger raised at the crowd.
branches.cn: 指认分支：从人群中举起的一根手指。

intro.en: Who is a bare question stem with almost no endings of its own, but it yields whom, whose and the free word whoever.
intro.cn: who 是几乎不带词尾的疑问词干，但它派生出 whom、whose 以及独立词 whoever。

latinIntro.en: The native stem is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show far relatives such as quis and qui.
latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词干属于日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目展示 quis、qui 这类远亲。

items.example: It works for subject and for relative clauses.
items.exampleCN: 它可作主语疑问，也可引导关系从句。

items.example: It appears in whoever as a whole word.
items.exampleCN: 它在 whoever 中以整词形式出现。

items.meaning: who is important or which is which

items.example: It turns a question into a shrug.
It joins who and ever as a single word.
items.exampleCN: 它把 who 与 ever 并成一个词。

latinEntries.example: It is the direct Latin parallel of who.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 who 在拉丁语中的直接对应词。

definition_zh: 无论谁；任何人；究竟是谁
definition_en: any person at all, no matter who, or an emphatic form of who in a question
core_image: 一扇敞开的门，门牌上写着无论谁来，都可以进来
scene: 老店主在门上挂了块牌子，写着不管是谁，只要把灯留着就能找到这里。Whoever arrives first should switch on the lights.
sceneCN: 这里 whoever 是「无论谁」（第 1 个义项：任何人都一样，不加区别）；句意为无论谁先到，都该把灯打开。那扇敞开、写着「谁来都行」的门，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Any person at all
senses.definition: used to say that any person, without exception, is meant
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示不加例外地指任何一个人
senses.example: Whoever arrives first should switch on the lights.
senses.exampleCN: 无论谁先到，都该把灯打开。
senses.why: The question word plus ever turns an open question into a door that accepts every answer.
senses.whyCN: 疑问词加上 ever，就把一个开放的提问变成一扇接受所有答案的门。

senses.title: No matter who did it
senses.definition: introducing a clause about an unknown person whose identity does not change the result
senses.definitionCN: 引导一个关于未知人物的从句，而此人是谁并不改变结果
senses.example: Whoever left the tap running should own up.
senses.exampleCN: 不管是谁让水龙头一直开着，都该承认。
senses.why: Here the clause stands at the head of the sentence, and the unknown person carries the blame.
senses.whyCN: 这里从句站在句首，那个未知的人承担着责任。

senses.title: An emphatic question
senses.definition: placed at the start of a question to add surprise or insistence
senses.definitionCN: 放在问句开头，增添惊讶或追问的语气
senses.example: Whoever told you that story was not telling the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 讲那个故事给你听的究竟是谁，他说的并不是真的。
senses.why: A plain who is neutral, and the extra ever adds weight and a raised eyebrow.
senses.whyCN: 单用 who 是中性，多出的 ever 则加了分量，也加了一条挑起的眉毛。

senses.title: The one who may
senses.definition: introducing a clause that acts as the subject or object of the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 引导一个充当句子主语或宾语的从句
senses.example: Give the key to whoever is on duty tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 把钥匙交给今晚值班的那个人。
senses.why: The clause names a role rather than a person, and whoever supplies a role that anyone might fill.
senses.whyCN: 这个从句命名的是一个角色而不是一个人，而 whoever 提供的正是一个谁都能填的角色。

intro.en: Whoever is a compound of who and ever, a pattern English uses for a whole set of open words such as whatever and whenever.
intro.cn: whoever 由 who 与 ever 复合而成，英语用这一模式造出了 whatever、whenever 等一整组开放词。

items.en: Hwa asked which person, and aefre meant at any time, the two running side by side as separate words.
items.cn: hwa 询问是哪个人，aefre 表示在任何时候，两者作为独立的词并列使用。

items.en: The pair was joined in writing, and swa hwa swa already carried the sense of any one at all.
items.cn: 两者在书写中合到一起，而更早的 swa hwa swa 已带有「任何人」之意。

items.en: From about the sixteenth century whoever appears as one word for any person and for an emphatic question.
items.cn: 大约自十六世纪起，whoever 作为单个词出现，表示任何人，也用于强调疑问。

items.en: The same model produced whatever, whenever and wherever, a whole family of open words.
items.cn: 同一模式造出了 whatever、whenever、wherever，构成一整个开放词家族。

items.en: Whomever survives in formal writing, but spoken English usually prefers whoever.
items.cn: whomever 仍见于正式书面语，但口语通常更爱用 whoever。

note.en: The first group gathers the other ever-compounds, the second the words that say any person or no matter.
note.cn: 第一组收其他带 ever 的复合词，第二组收表示「任何人」「不管」的说法。

entries.definition: Anything at all, or no matter what.
At any time, or every time that.
In any place at all.
The object form of whoever in formal writing.
Any person without a name.
The same idea in everyday speech.
Without paying attention to who or what.

normalIntro.en: Whoever is who plus ever, and the ever is the part that throws the door open.
normalIntro.cn: whoever 就是 who 加 ever，真正把门推开的是后面的 ever。

normal.en: Who asks a name, and ever answers it is anybody, so the pair opens the door.
normal.cn: who 问名字，ever 回答「谁都是」，两个一凑门就开了。

normal.en: Whatever, whoever, whenever, wherever: the same ever runs through the whole family.
normal.cn: whatever、whoever、whenever、wherever：同一个 ever 贯穿整个家族。

normal.en: Before a verb it is a subject, before a role it is a filler.
normal.cn: 放在动词前是主语，放在角色前是填空的人。

normal.en: Give it to whoever asks takes an object position without the old m.
normal.cn: give it to whoever asks 用宾位却不用旧的 m。

normal.en: Spoken English drops whomever and keeps whoever.
normal.cn: 口语丢掉 whomever，只留 whoever。

abstract.en: See a door standing open with the light left on.
abstract.cn: 看见一扇开着的门，灯还亮着。

abstract.en: Feel a blank space where a name could be printed.
abstract.cn: 感觉有个空白处，本来可以印一个名字。

abstract.en: Hear a hand knocking before the face is seen.
abstract.cn: 听见敲门声，脸还没出现。

examples.en: Whoever finishes last washes the cups.
examples.cn: 谁最后吃完谁洗杯子。

examples.en: Whoever left the window open, please close it now.
examples.cn: 不管是谁开的窗，请现在就关上。

examples.en: She gives free bread to whoever comes before noon.
examples.cn: 中午之前来的人，她都免费给面包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呼艾沃」——呼一声，艾沃也好、谁都好，来了就算数。

root: 古英语 hwa（谁）+ aefre（任何时候）在中古英语合写，十六世纪起成为单词 whoever；同族有 whomever、whatever、whenever。

sensesIntro.en: The word takes an open question and closes it for every possible answer, then moves from the subject of a clause to a role anyone could fill.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词把开放的提问对所有可能的答案一律关上，再从从句主语移向谁都能填的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open door with the light on, a name still blank.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇开着的门、亮着的灯，名字仍空着。

branches.en: The open-door branch: whoever arrives first turns on the lights.
branches.cn: 开门分支：无论谁先到都把灯打开。

branches.en: The blame branch: whoever left the tap running.
branches.cn: 责任分支：不管是谁没关水龙头。

branches.en: The surprise branch: whoever told you that.
branches.cn: 惊讶分支：说那话的究竟是谁。

branches.en: The role branch: the key goes to whoever is on duty.
branches.cn: 角色分支：钥匙交给值班的那个人。

branches.en: The any-person branch: anyone, spoken plainly.
branches.cn: 任一分枝：也就是平常说的任何人。

intro.en: Whoever is a compound of the question stem who and the free word ever, and the second half is what carries the meaning of any and no matter.
intro.cn: whoever 是疑问词干 who 与自由词 ever 的复合，后半部分才承载「任何」「不管」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native Germanic, so there is no Latin source; the Latin entries below offer the closest parallel expressions.
latinIntro.cn: 前后两半都是本土日耳曼词，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出最接近的对应说法。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 whatever 与 whenever。

items.example: It stands as one word in modern use.
items.exampleCN: 现代用法中它是一个词。

items.meaning: the person who may want it

latinEntries.example: It is built from quis plus -cumque, the same doubling.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它由 quis 加 -cumque 构成，是同一种叠加。

definition_zh: 全部的；完整的；整个的；完整的事物；整体
definition_en: complete, with no part missing or broken, and the complete thing taken as one
core_image: 一只没被切开的圆苹果，皮从蒂到顶连成一圈，光亮完整
scene: 孩子捧着一只没切过的圆苹果，从皮到核全都还在，一口咬下去才第一次破开。He ate the whole apple, including the core.
sceneCN: 这里 whole 是「全部的、完整的」（第 1 个义项：没有任何部分缺失或被切开）；句意为他吃掉了整个苹果，连核也没剩。那只从皮到蒂连成一圈、还没破开的圆苹果，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Complete, with nothing missing
senses.definition: having every part present, with nothing taken away or broken off
senses.definitionCN: 各部分都在，没有被取走或折断的地方
senses.example: He ate the whole apple, including the core.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整个苹果都吃了，连核也没剩。
senses.why: The oldest sense is sound and unbroken, so completeness is the base of everything else.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是健全、未破损，因此「完整」是其他一切意思的基础。

senses.title: The entire amount or period
senses.definition: used before a singular noun to mean all of it, the entire amount or time
senses.definitionCN: 用在单数名词前，表示该事物的全部或整段时间
senses.example: She spent the whole morning cleaning the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她一整个上午都在打扫厨房。
senses.why: English prefers one whole noun to all the noun, so the adjective slides into counting.
senses.whyCN: 英语更爱说一个完整的名词，而不是「所有的」名词，于是这个形容词滑向了计数。

senses.title: The thing as one unit
senses.definition: the complete object or set seen as a single thing rather than as parts
senses.definitionCN: 把完整的东西或一整套看成单一之物，而不是各部分之和
senses.example: The parts were shipped separately and the whole was put together on site.
senses.exampleCN: 零件分别运来，整个东西在工地上组装起来。
senses.why: The noun keeps the picture of an unbroken object and simply removes the word for its parts.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时保留了那个未破开的物体形象，只是把「部分」的说法从视野里去掉。

senses.title: In good condition
senses.definition: in old or formal use, healthy and not damaged in body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 在旧式或正式用法中，指身心没有受损、健康无病
senses.example: The doctor said his mind was still whole after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说他摔倒后神志仍然健全。
senses.why: The Germanic root meant sound and healthy, and the physical sense of unbroken grew out of it.
senses.whyCN: 日耳曼语词根本来指健康无碍，未破损的物理意义正是从这里长出来的。

senses.title: In the fixed phrases
senses.definition: in on the whole meaning generally, and as a whole meaning together
senses.definitionCN: 用于 on the whole（总的来说）与 as a whole（作为一个整体）
senses.example: On the whole the plan worked well.
senses.exampleCN: 总的来说，这个计划运行得不错。
senses.why: The noun inside these phrases stands for everything counted together, an old habit of adding up.
senses.whyCN: 这些说法里的名词代表把一切加总起来，这是一种古老的计数习惯。

intro.en: Whole goes back to Old English hal, meaning sound, healthy and unhurt, the same root as heal and healthy.
intro.cn: whole 可上溯到古英语 hal，意为健全、健康、未受伤，与 heal、healthy 同根。

items.en: The root meant sound and without damage, describing a healthy body more than a full set.
items.cn: 这个词根表示健全、无损伤，更多描述健康的身体而非完备的集合。

items.en: Hal meant whole and healthy, and gave the verb haelian, to heal.
items.cn: hal 表示完整、健康，并派生动词 haelian（治愈）。

items.en: The w was added in spelling by analogy with who, and hol came to mean entire rather than sound.
items.cn: 中古英语时期受 who 影响在拼写中加入 w，hol 的词义也从「健全」转向「整个」。

items.en: The sense of complete and entire became the main one, while healthy kept the old health sense.
items.cn: 「完整、全部」成为主要意思，而健康义则由 healthy 继承下来。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as on the whole and as a whole gave the word a summing-up role.
items.cn: on the whole 与 as a whole 这类固定说法赋予它做总结的角色。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike words that differ by one letter or sound, the second the words for complete and for a total.
note.cn: 第一组收只差一个字母或读音的形近词，第二组收表示完整与总体。

entries.definition: A gap or opening, pronounced exactly the same.
To make healthy again, from the same old root.
Completely, the adverb of whole.
The spelling that put a w into whole.
Complete, often of an amount or a span.
The full amount counted together.
The result of adding the parts up.

normalIntro.en: Whole is the picture of an apple with no bite taken, and the silent w is the only trick in it.
normalIntro.cn: whole 就是一只没被咬过的苹果，唯一的陷阱是那个不发音的 w。

normal.en: Whole and hole sound identical; the w is decoration, the meaning is completeness.
normal.cn: whole 与 hole 读音相同；w 只是装饰，意思仍是完整。

normal.en: Heal and whole come from one family: to heal is to make sound again.
normal.cn: heal 与 whole 同族：治愈就是让它重新健全。

normal.en: On the whole is the same word used to add everything up.
normal.cn: on the whole 就是用这个词把一切加起来。

normal.en: Whole milk has not had the cream removed.
normal.cn: 全脂牛奶就是没有把奶油取走的牛奶。

normal.en: W-h-o-l-e keeps who at the start, why is a question you should skip.
normal.cn: whole 以 who 开头，不必追究那个 w 的来由。

abstract.en: Feel the smooth unbroken skin of an apple in the palm.
abstract.cn: 感觉掌心里苹果那层光滑未破的皮。

abstract.en: Hear a sound with no crack in it.
abstract.cn: 听一个没有裂纹的声音。

abstract.en: See a circle closed at the point where it started.
abstract.cn: 看见一个圆在起点处合拢。

examples.en: The whole village came out to watch the fireworks.
examples.cn: 全村的人都出来看烟花。

examples.en: On the whole, I think we made the right choice.
examples.cn: 总的来说，我认为我们的选择是对的。

examples.en: Two halves make a whole.
examples.cn: 两个半块合成一个整体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「后」——后面什么都还在，一个不少，所以是完整的。

root: 日耳曼语词根（健全、无伤）→ 古英语 hal（完整、健康）→ 中古英语 whole（受 who 影响加 w）→ 现代英语 whole；同族有 heal、healthy、wholly。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a body that is sound and unhurt, ships the physical sense of unbroken, then takes up all of a period, all of a thing, and the art of summing up.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从健全无伤的身体开始，随后带出未破损的物理意义，再接上整段时间、整个事物以及做总结的功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an apple with no bite taken, the skin unbroken.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没被咬过的苹果，皮是连着的。

branches.en: The apple branch: eaten whole, core and all.
branches.cn: 苹果分支：整个吃掉，连核也在内。

branches.en: The whole-morning branch: one long stretch of time.
branches.cn: 整个上午的分支：一整段时间。

branches.en: The assembly branch: parts shipped, the whole built on site.
branches.cn: 组装分支：零件运来，整体在现场装成。

branches.en: The health branch: a mind still whole after a fall.
branches.cn: 健康分支：摔倒后神志仍然健全。

branches.en: The summing branch: on the whole the plan worked.
branches.cn: 总结分支：总的来说计划可行。

intro.en: Whole is a free root with a silent w, and it builds adverbs and compounds with -ly, -ness and a first element such as whole- in wholesale.
intro.cn: whole 是带不发音 w 的自由词根，可用 -ly、-ness 派生副词与名词，也能作为前项构成 wholesale 一类复合词。

latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目给出常用来翻译它的借入词。

definition_zh: 完全地；全部地；整个地
definition_en: completely and entirely, with no part left out and nothing held back
core_image: 一整桶水倒过来，一滴不剩全倒进盆里
scene: 她把桶整个翻过来，水全倒进盆里，桶底一滴也不剩。I wholly agree with your second point.
sceneCN: 这里 wholly 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项：没有一点遗漏、没有保留）；句意为我完全同意你的第二点。那只被整个翻过来、一滴不剩的水桶，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: To the last part
senses.definition: in every part, so that nothing at all is excluded
senses.definitionCN: 在每一个部分上都是如此，没有任何东西被排除在外
senses.example: I wholly agree with your second point.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全同意你的第二点。
senses.why: The adverb simply says that the complete object is involved, not a part of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是说明涉及的是完整的对象，而不是它的一部分。

senses.title: Entirely, before an adjective
senses.definition: used to strengthen an adjective, meaning quite or utterly
senses.definitionCN: 用于加强形容词，意为「相当」「完全」
senses.example: The whole plan was wholly unexpected to the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划对员工来说完全出乎意料。
senses.why: Placed before an adjective it works like an intensifier, wiping out the middle ground.
senses.whyCN: 放在形容词之前，它起加强作用，把中间地带抹掉。

senses.title: Not partly
senses.definition: in a negative sentence, used to mean not completely, often with a hint of doubt
senses.definitionCN: 在否定句中表示「不完全」，常带一点保留或怀疑
senses.example: I am not wholly sure that the date is right.
senses.exampleCN: 我并不十分确定日期是对的。
senses.why: A plain no would be too hard, and the word lets a little room into the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 直截了当地否定太生硬，这个词给句子留出一点余地。

senses.title: Owned by one party
senses.definition: in business use, describing a company owned in full by another
senses.definitionCN: 在商业用法中，描述一家公司被另一方全部持有
senses.example: The factory is wholly owned by the parent company in Shanghai.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂由上海的母公司全资拥有。
senses.why: The same idea of completeness moved into company records, where shares are either all or part.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「完整」的想法进入了公司账目，因为股份要么全部要么部分。

intro.en: Wholly is whole plus the adverb ending -ly, made from Old English hal, sound and complete.
intro.cn: wholly 是 whole 加副词词尾 -ly，其源头是表示健全、完整的古英语 hal。

items.en: Hal meant sound and healthy, and the adverb halice meant in a sound or complete way.
items.cn: hal 表示健全、健康，副词 halice 表示以健全或完整的方式。

items.en: With the added w in whole, the adverb appeared as holliche and later wholy.
items.cn: 随着 whole 加入 w，副词写作 holliche，之后又变为 wholy。

items.en: The spelling settled as wholly, keeping the l of whole before the ending.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 wholly，在词尾前保留了 whole 的 l。

items.en: Its chief work became strengthening adjectives such as wholly different and wholly unexpected.
items.cn: 它主要的用途变成加强 wholly different、wholly unexpected 这类形容词。

items.en: Business writing gave it the fixed use of full ownership, as in wholly owned.
items.cn: 商业写作给了它「全资」这一固定用法，如 wholly owned。

note.en: The first group gathers adverbs of completeness that look or sound alike, the second the words that stress a whole without parts.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的「完全」类副词，第二组收强调整体无部分之分的词。

entries.definition: The adjective this adverb is built from.
Sacred, pronounced almost the same.
Full of holes, spelled differently.
Selling in bulk, built on the same base.
In every part, the everyday choice.
As a whole, often before a negative.
To the extreme, with strong feeling.

normalIntro.en: Wholly looks like holy and holey, so the doubled l and the meaning of the base word are the two things to hold on to.
normalIntro.cn: wholly 看着像 holy 和 holey，所以抓住两件事：双写的 l，以及原词「完整」的意思。

normal.en: Whole plus ly means in a complete way, and the l doubles before the ending.
normal.cn: whole 加 ly 表示以完整的方式，加词尾时 l 要双写。

normal.en: Holy is sacred, holey has holes, wholly means entirely.
normal.cn: holy 是神圣，holey 是多洞，wholly 是完全。

normal.en: Put it before an adjective to shut the door on any middle ground.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前，就堵住了任何中间地带。

normal.en: I am not wholly sure leaves a crack of doubt open.
normal.cn: I am not wholly sure 还留着一道怀疑的缝。

normal.en: Wholly owned is a set phrase in company papers.
normal.cn: wholly owned 是公司文件中的固定说法。

abstract.en: Feel a bucket turned over with nothing left inside.
abstract.cn: 感觉一只桶被翻过来，里面什么也没剩。

abstract.en: See a shade of difference squeezed out of two colours.
abstract.cn: 看见两种颜色之间那点差别被挤走。

abstract.en: Hear a yes with no pause after it.
abstract.cn: 听一个后面没有停顿的「是」。

examples.en: The two brothers are wholly different in temper.
examples.cn: 这两兄弟的脾气完全不同。

examples.en: I am not wholly convinced by that argument.
examples.cn: 我并不完全信服那个论点。

examples.en: The shop is wholly owned by the family.
examples.cn: 这家店由这家人全资拥有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「后利」——后面把所有的利都收全了，一点不剩，就是完全地。

root: 古英语 hal（健全、完整）+ 副词词尾 -ly → 中古英语 holliche → 现代英语 wholly；同族有 whole、wholeness。

sensesIntro.en: The word says that all of something is involved, then serves to strengthen an adjective, then softens a negative, and finally fixes itself in company records.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词说明涉及的是全部，接着用来加强形容词，再用来软化否定，最后固定在公司账目里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tipped bucket with not one drop left behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只倒空的桶，一滴也没留下。

chain: A DOUBLED L AT THE END

branches.en: The agreement branch: wholly agreeing with a point.
branches.cn: 同意分支：完全同意某一点。

branches.en: The intensifier branch: an entirely unexpected plan.
branches.cn: 加强分支：完全出乎意料的计划。

branches.en: The doubt branch: not wholly sure of a date.
branches.cn: 怀疑分支：对日期并不十分确定。

branches.en: The company branch: a wholly owned factory.
branches.cn: 公司分支：一家全资工厂。

branches.en: The no-parts branch: no middle ground allowed.
branches.cn: 无部分分支：不允许中间地带。

intro.en: Wholly is a regular adverb built with -ly, and the doubled l is only a spelling rule of that suffix.
intro.cn: wholly 是用 -ly 构成的规则副词，双写的 l 只是该后缀的拼写规则。

latinIntro.en: The base word is native Germanic and has no Latin source; the Latin entries below show the common borrowed equivalents.
latinIntro.cn: 词基本身是本土日耳曼词，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出常见的借入对应词。

items.exampleCN: 它是这个副词的基本词。

items.example: A fixed frame from business writing.
items.exampleCN: 商业写作中的固定框架。

items.example: The negative leaves a little doubt.
items.exampleCN: 这个否定留下一点怀疑。
