definition_zh: 谁（宾格）；…的那个人（宾格关系代词）
definition_en: the object form of who, used after a verb or a preposition and in careful relative clauses
core_image: 一只手把某个人指给另一个人看，被指的人站在前面，动作落在他身上
scene: 律师翻着名单，问在场的人这封信究竟寄给谁，问到的人却一声不响。To whom should I address this letter?
sceneCN: 这里 whom 是「谁（宾格）」（第 1 个义项：作动词或介词的宾语时用的形式）；句意为我该把这封信寄给谁呢。那只把动作引到某人身上的指向，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Asking for the object
senses.definition: the object form of who, used when the unknown person receives the action of the verb
senses.definitionCN: who 的宾格形式，在未知的人承受动作时使用
senses.example: Whom did you meet at the station?
senses.exampleCN: 你在车站遇见了谁？
senses.why: English once kept a full set of case endings, and this is the one survivor in common use.
senses.whyCN: 英语曾保留完整的格词尾，而这是日常用法中唯一存活下来的那个。

senses.title: After a preposition
senses.definition: used directly after a preposition such as to, with or for, where who is not allowed in careful style
senses.definitionCN: 直接用于 to、with、for 等介词之后，在严谨文体中此处不用 who
senses.example: To whom should I address this letter?
senses.exampleCN: 我该把这封信寄给谁呢？
senses.why: A preposition needs an object right after it, and the old object form still fills that slot.
senses.whyCN: 介词后面需要宾语，而这个古老的宾格形式仍能占住那个位置。

senses.title: The relative object form
senses.definition: in a relative clause, referring back to a person who is the object of the clause
senses.definitionCN: 在关系从句中回指一个人，而此人在从句里是宾语
senses.example: The painter whom we met last year has died.
senses.exampleCN: 我们去年见过的那位画家去世了。
senses.why: When the person is acted upon inside the clause, careful writers choose whom.
senses.whyCN: 当此人在从句中承受动作时，严谨的作者会选用 whom。

senses.title: In formal lists and counts
senses.definition: in formal writing, used after of to pick a group out of a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 在正式书面语中放在 of 之后，表示从更大群体中挑出的一群
senses.example: The team has three members, two of whom are engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队有三名成员，其中两名是工程师。
senses.why: Counting people with of needs the object form, so the word survives in statistics and reports.
senses.whyCN: 用 of 来数人需要宾格，所以这个词在统计与报告中仍然存活。

intro.en: Whom is the old dative and accusative of who, from Old English hwam, the case forms of hwa.
intro.cn: whom 是 who 古老的与格和宾格形式，来自古英语 hwa 的格形式 hwam。

items.en: The question stem took different endings for subject, object and possessor in every old Germanic language.
items.cn: 在所有古老的日耳曼语言中，疑问词干都会按主语、宾语、所有者换上不同词尾。

items.en: Hwa was the subject form and hwam the form used for the object and after prepositions.
items.cn: hwa 是主格，hwam 用于宾语以及介词之后。

items.en: The ending weakened to whom, and careful writers kept it while speech began to drop it.
items.cn: 词尾弱化为 whom，严谨的作者仍保留它，而口语已开始丢弃。

items.en: After a preposition whom stayed firm in writing, as in to whom and of whom.
items.cn: 在介词之后，whom 在书面语中稳稳站住，如 to whom、of whom。

items.en: Today spoken English usually says who, and whom is a mark of careful or dated style.
items.cn: 如今口语通常说 who，而 whom 是严谨或略显陈旧文体的标志。

note.en: The first group gathers the other case forms of the same stem, the second the plain relative words that can replace it.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干的其他格形式，第二组收可以替代它的朴素关系词。

entries.definition: The subject form of the same word.
The possessive form, asking about ownership.
The object form of whoever.
A sudden wish, unrelated in origin.
A plain relative word, no case endings needed.
A relative word for things rather than people.
An unnamed person, often the answer to whom.

normalIntro.en: Whom is who with an m, and the m is a memory of the old case endings English once had.
normalIntro.cn: whom 就是带 m 的 who，这个 m 是英语曾经那套格词尾留下的记忆。

normal.en: Him and them end in m too, and all three are object forms.
normal.cn: him 和 them 也是 m 结尾，三者都是宾格。

normal.en: If him fits the gap, then whom fits as well.
normal.cn: 如果那个空里能放 him，那么也能放 whom。

normal.en: After to, with, of and for, whom is the safe choice in writing.
normal.cn: 写在 to、with、of、for 之后，whom 是稳妥的选择。

normal.en: Two of whom are engineers: the of makes the case clear.
normal.cn: two of whom are engineers 中的 of 把格说得很清楚。

normal.en: In speech, who has almost taken over, so whom is mostly ink.
normal.cn: 口语里 who 几乎接管了一切，所以 whom 多半只出现在纸上。

abstract.en: Feel an action landing on a person who does nothing back.
abstract.cn: 感觉一个动作落在某人身上，而那人毫无反击。

abstract.en: See a finger pointed by one person at another.
abstract.cn: 看见一个人把手指向另一个人。

abstract.en: Hear a name asked for by a preposition.
abstract.cn: 听见介词在追问一个名字。

examples.en: The lecturer whom everyone respected has retired.
examples.cn: 那位人人尊敬的讲师已经退休了。

examples.en: With whom did you travel to the north?
examples.cn: 你和谁一起去了北方？

examples.en: Ten students took part, most of whom came from the village.
examples.cn: 十名学生参加，其中大多数来自村里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呼姆」——呼一声姆，姆被叫过去，是被动的那个，所以是宾格。

root: 日耳曼语疑问词干 → 古英语 hwam（宾格、与格）→ 中古英语 whom → 现代英语 whom；同族有 who、whose、whomever。

sensesIntro.en: The word marks a person who receives the action, keeps that work after a preposition, carries it into relative clauses, and finally into formal counts.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词标记承受动作的人，在介词后保持这一功能，再带进关系从句，最后进入正式的计数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing at someone, the action falling on that person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指指向某人，动作落在那人身上。

branches.en: The question branch: whom did you meet at the station.
branches.cn: 发问分支：你在车站遇见了谁。

branches.en: The preposition branch: to whom should I write.
branches.cn: 介词分支：我该写给谁。

branches.en: The relative branch: the painter whom we met.
branches.cn: 关系分支：我们见过的那位画家。

branches.en: The counting branch: two of whom are engineers.
branches.cn: 计数分支：其中两位是工程师。

branches.en: The object branch: him fits, so whom fits.
branches.cn: 宾语分支：能放 him，也就能放 whom。

intro.en: Whom is not built with a suffix but is a case form of the question stem, and it feeds the compound whomever.
intro.cn: whom 不是用后缀构成的，而是疑问词干的一个格形式，它还派生出复合词 whomever。

latinIntro.en: The native stem has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show how the same case work is done with quis and quem.
latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词干没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目展示 quis、quem 如何承担同样的格功能。

items.example: The preposition fixes the case in writing.
items.exampleCN: 介词在书面语中固定了口格。

items.example: It survives in reports and lists.
items.exampleCN: 它存活于报告与名单中。

items.meaning: which person to do something with
items.example: A small clause with an infinitive.
items.exampleCN: 一个带动词不定式的小句。

items.example: It pairs the case form with ever.
items.exampleCN: 它把宾格形式与 ever 配对。

latinEntries.example: It is the exact Latin accusative of quis.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 quis 的拉丁语宾格的精确对应。

definition_zh: 谁的；其；（关系代词）…的（人或物）
definition_en: the possessive form of who, asking which person owns something, or linking a noun to its owner
core_image: 一只被落在长椅上的手套，旁边的人都低头看自己的手，看谁少了一只
scene: 长椅上孤零零落着一只红手套，路过的人都抬起手来数一数自己的手指，问这是谁的。Whose gloves are these on the bench?
sceneCN: 这里 whose 是「谁的」（第 1 个义项：询问某物属于哪个人）；句意为长椅上这些手套是谁的。所有人都低头数自己手指的那一幕，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: the girl whose bag was stolen
a house whose windows face south

senses.title: Asking who owns it
senses.definition: used in a question to ask which person something belongs to
senses.definitionCN: 在问句中询问某物属于哪个人
senses.example: Whose gloves are these on the bench?
senses.exampleCN: 长椅上这些手套是谁的？
senses.why: The word carries the owner into the question before the thing is even named.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在东西还没被说出来之前，就把所有者带进了问句。

senses.title: A relative word for an owner
senses.definition: in a relative clause, linking a person to something that belongs to them or is tied to them
senses.definitionCN: 在关系从句中把一个人与其所属之物或有关系之物连起来
senses.example: The girl whose bag was stolen reported it at once.
senses.exampleCN: 包被偷的那个女孩立刻报了案。
senses.why: Here the clause cannot stand alone, and the word works as a bridge from person to possession.
senses.whyCN: 这里从句不能独立成立，而这个词充当从人通往所属物的桥。

senses.title: Used of things in formal style
senses.definition: in formal writing, used to join a thing to one of its features, where of which is also possible
senses.definitionCN: 在正式书面语中把某物与其特征相连，也可换成 of which 结构
senses.example: They live in a house whose windows face south.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在一所窗户朝南的房子里。
senses.why: Strictly the word belongs to people, but careful English lets it stand for things with a feature.
senses.whyCN: 严格说来这个词属于人，但严谨的英语也允许它指带有某特征的事物。

senses.title: In set questions
senses.definition: in fixed phrases such as whose turn or whose fault
senses.definitionCN: 用于 whose turn、whose fault 等固定说法
senses.example: Whose turn is it to wash up tonight?
senses.exampleCN: 今晚轮到谁洗碗？
senses.why: Short questions of ownership turned into everyday formulas with the word frozen inside.
senses.whyCN: 关于归属的短问句固化为日常套话，而这个词就冻在里面。

intro.en: Whose is the old genitive of who, from Old English hwaes, and it kept a role that who and whom lost.
intro.cn: whose 是 who 古老的所有格，来自古英语 hwaes，它保住了 who 与 whom 已经失去的一项功能。

items.en: The question stem carried a genitive ending meaning of whom in the old Germanic languages.
items.cn: 在古老的日耳曼语言中，疑问词干带有一个表示「谁的」的所有格词尾。

items.en: Hwaes was the genitive of hwa and stood before the thing owned.
items.cn: hwaes 是 hwa 的所有格，放在被拥有之物之前。

items.en: The form became whos and then whose, and it spread from questions into relative clauses.
items.cn: 词形先后成为 whos 与 whose，并从问句扩展到关系从句。

items.en: Unlike who and whom, whose never lost its place, because no other word could do its work as neatly.
items.cn: 与 who、whom 不同，whose 从未失去位置，因为没有别的词能如此利落地承担它的功能。

items.en: Careful writers began using it for things as well, as a shorter form of of which.
items.cn: 严谨的作者开始把它也用于事物，作为 of which 的简短形式。

note.en: The first group gathers the other forms of the same question stem, the second ways of saying that something belongs.
note.cn: 第一组收同一疑问词干的其他形式，第二组收表示归属的其他说法。

entries.definition: The subject form of the same word.
The object form of the same word.
An informal spelling of who is, without the apostrophe.
Of any person at all, the doubled form.
The longer way to attach a feature to a thing.
Being the property of someone.
The person a whose question is looking for.

normalIntro.en: Whose is who plus the old possessive ending, and the missing apostrophe is what separates it from the contraction of who is.
normalIntro.cn: whose 是 who 加古老的所有格词尾，而少了那个撇号，正是它与 who is 缩写的区别。

normal.en: His and its own the thing; whose asks who owns it.
normal.cn: his 和 its 是占据，whose 是追问谁在占据。

normal.en: No apostrophe, because the s is an ending, not a missing letter.
normal.cn: 不写撇号，因为这个 s 是词尾，不是省掉的字母。

normal.en: The phrase「the girl whose bag was stolen」keeps the owner in the subject position.
normal.cn: 「the girl whose bag was stolen」把所有者放在主语位置上。

normal.en: Whose turn and whose fault are two everyday formulas.
normal.cn: whose turn 与 whose fault 是两个日常套话。

normal.en: For things, of which is longer but safer in exams.
normal.cn: 指物时，of which 更长，但在考试中更保险。

abstract.en: See one red glove alone on a bench.
abstract.cn: 看见长椅上孤零零一只红手套。

abstract.en: Feel a hand counting its own fingers, just in case.
abstract.cn: 感觉一只手在偷偷数自己的手指。

abstract.en: Hear a question that asks for an owner, not a name.
abstract.cn: 听见一个追问所有者而非名字的问句。

examples.en: Whose coat is hanging behind the door?
examples.cn: 门后挂着的是谁的外套？

examples.en: The boy whose father teaches music plays the violin well.
examples.cn: 父亲教音乐的那个男孩小提琴拉得很好。

examples.en: It is a small town whose streets are all named after flowers.
examples.cn: 那是个小镇，街道都以花命名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呼兹」——呼一声兹，兹的东西就是兹的，问的就是谁的。

root: 日耳曼语疑问词干 + 所有格词尾 → 古英语 hwaes → 中古英语 whose → 现代英语 whose；同族有 who、whom、whosever。

sensesIntro.en: The word asks who owns a thing, then links a person to what belongs to them, then reaches out to things as a short form of of which, and finally freezes in set questions.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先问东西属于谁，再把人与其所属物连起来，又作为 of which 的短形式伸向事物，最后冻在固定问法里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one red glove on a bench, and everyone counting their own fingers.
core.cn: 核心意象：长椅上的一只红手套，以及人人都在数自己的手指。

branches.en: The ownership branch: whose gloves are these.
branches.cn: 归属分支：这些手套是谁的。

branches.en: The relative branch: the girl whose bag was stolen.
branches.cn: 关系分支：包被偷的那个女孩。

branches.en: The thing branch: a house whose windows face south.
branches.cn: 事物分支：窗户朝南的房子。

branches.en: The formula branch: whose turn to wash up.
branches.cn: 套话分支：轮到谁洗碗。

branches.en: The owner branch: a question looking for a person.
branches.cn: 所有者分支：寻找一个人的问句。

intro.en: Whose is a case form of the question stem rather than a suffixed word, and it becomes whosever by adding ever.
intro.cn: whose 是疑问词干的格形式而非带后缀的词，加上 ever 后成为 whosever。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native Germanic, so there is no Latin source; the Latin entries below show the possessive parallel with cuius.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目展示 cuius 这一所有格对应形式。

items.meaning: the owner inside a longer phrase

latinEntries.example: It is the genitive of quis, the exact parallel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 quis 的所有格，精确对应。

definition_zh: 为什么；何以；原因；理由
definition_en: the question word for a reason, and the reason or purpose itself
core_image: 一个孩子拽着大人的袖子，抬头追问那一个问题：为什么
scene: 孩子指着天上慢慢走的云，一遍遍追问它究竟为什么不肯停下来。Why did the train stop in the middle of the field?
sceneCN: 这里 why 是「为什么」（第 1 个义项：询问原因的疑问词）；句意为火车为什么停在田野中间。孩子拽着袖子抬头追问的那一幕，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Asking for a reason
senses.definition: used at the start of a question to ask for the cause or the purpose of something
senses.definitionCN: 放在问句开头，询问某事的原因或目的
senses.example: Why did the train stop in the middle of the field?
senses.exampleCN: 火车为什么停在田野中间？
senses.why: The word asks for the thread that leads back from an event to its cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个词追问的是从一件事牵回其起因的那根线。

senses.title: In the phrase why not
senses.definition: used to suggest something or to agree cheerfully to a proposal
senses.definitionCN: 用来提议某事，或愉快地同意一个建议
senses.example: Why not take the early bus and be there before lunch?
senses.exampleCN: 何不坐早班车，午饭前就能到？
senses.why: A question turned into a gentle push, since the missing answer is obviously yes.
senses.whyCN: 一个问句变成了温和的推动，因为缺的那个答案显然是「好」。

senses.title: Introducing a clause after reason
senses.definition: used after the noun reason to introduce the clause that explains it
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词 reason 之后，引导解释它的从句
senses.example: Nobody knows the reason why the birds left so early.
senses.exampleCN: 没人知道这些鸟为什么这么早就离开。
senses.why: The question word becomes a relative word, tying the general noun to its explanation.
senses.whyCN: 这个疑问词变成关系词，把「理由」这个笼统名词与它的解释系在一起。

senses.title: The reason itself
senses.definition: as a noun, the cause or explanation of something, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指某事的原因或解释，常用复数
senses.example: He never explained the whys of his sudden move.
senses.exampleCN: 他从未解释自己突然搬走的各种原因。
senses.why: A question word was turned into a noun, so the asking itself became the thing asked about.
senses.whyCN: 一个疑问词被变成名词，于是「发问」本身成了被追问的对象。

senses.title: In an exclamation
senses.definition: used at the beginning of an exclamation to express surprise or protest
senses.definitionCN: 放在感叹句开头，表示惊讶或抗议
senses.example: Why, that is the very book I lost last week!
senses.exampleCN: 哎呀，那正是我上星期丢的那本书！
senses.why: The same word softened an objection, and in speech it became a small surprised noise.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词能缓和反驳，在口语中又成了小小的惊讶声。

intro.en: Why descends from Old English hwy, the instrumental case of the question stem, literally by what.
intro.cn: why 源自古英语 hwy，是疑问词干的工具格，字面意思是「凭着什么」。

items.en: The old stem had a case for means or instrument, which answered the question by what agency.
items.cn: 古老的词干有一个表示手段或工具的格，回答「凭借什么」这一问题。

items.en: Hwy and hwi were the instrumental forms, and they were used to ask for a cause.
items.cn: hwy 与 hwi 是工具格形式，用来追问原因。

items.en: The form settled as why, and the word also began to stand after the noun reason.
items.cn: 词形固定为 why，这个词也开始出现在名词 reason 之后。

items.en: Why not became a polite suggestion, and why on earth added force to surprise.
items.cn: why not 成为礼貌的建议，why on earth 则为惊讶加上力量。

items.en: The plural whys turned the question into a noun, as in the whys of a decision.
items.cn: 复数 whys 把提问变成名词，如 the whys of a decision。

note.en: The first group gathers the other question words of the same family, the second the words that give reasons back.
note.cn: 第一组收同族其他疑问词，第二组收给出原因的回答词。

entries.definition: The question word for a thing.
The question word for a person.
The question word for manner, not cause.
The question word for place.
The word that answers a why question.
The explanation a why question looks for.
An old formal word meaning for what reason.

normalIntro.en: Why is a single syllable that always points backwards, from a fact to its cause.
normalIntro.cn: why 是一个总是往回指的音节，从一件事指回它的原因。

normal.en: Why shares its w with what and where, the whole family of questions.
normal.cn: why 与 what、where 共用 w，同属一整个疑问家族。

normal.en: Y is the fork in the road, the point where you ask which way and why.
normal.cn: 字母 y 像岔路口，正好是你问「为什么走这条」的地方。

normal.en: Why not is a yes wearing a question mark.
normal.cn: why not 就是一个戴着问号的「好」。

normal.en: The reason why keeps the question glued to its noun.
normal.cn: the reason why 把问句粘在它的名词后面。

normal.en: The whys of a thing are its reasons, counted up.
normal.cn: 一件事的 whys 就是它的种种缘由，被一条条数出来。

abstract.en: Feel the tug on a sleeve that will not stop.
abstract.cn: 感觉袖子上那一下不肯停的拉扯。

abstract.en: See a cloud that refuses to say where it is going.
abstract.cn: 看见一朵云不肯说它要去哪。

abstract.en: Hear a question that has no floor beneath it.
abstract.cn: 听见一个底下没有地板的问题。

examples.en: Why is the light still on upstairs?
examples.cn: 楼上为什么还亮着灯？

examples.en: I cannot explain why she left so suddenly.
examples.cn: 我无法解释她为什么走得那么突然。

examples.en: Why not ask the teacher to look at it again?
examples.cn: 何不让老师再看一遍呢？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外」——往外看半天也想不通，只好问一句为什么。

root: 日耳曼语疑问词干的工具格（凭何）→ 古英语 hwy → 中古英语 why → 现代英语 why；同族有 what、where、how。

sensesIntro.en: The word asks what led to something, becomes a cheerful suggestion, then a relative word, then the reason itself, and at last a small surprised opening.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词追问是什么引出了某事，接着变成愉快的建议、关系词、原因本身，最后成为一声小小的惊讶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child pulling a sleeve, asking one question again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子拉扯袖子，把同一个问题再问一遍。

branches.en: The cause branch: why the train stopped in a field.
branches.cn: 原因分支：火车为何停在田野里。

branches.en: The suggestion branch: why not take the early bus.
branches.cn: 建议分支：何不坐早班车。

branches.en: The linking branch: the reason why the birds left.
branches.cn: 连接分支：鸟早早离开的原因。

branches.en: The noun branch: the whys of a sudden move.
branches.cn: 名词分支：突然搬走的种种原因。

branches.en: The exclamation branch: why, that is my book.
branches.cn: 感叹分支：哎呀，那是我的书。

intro.en: Why is a bare question word with no affixes of its own, and its only derived form is the plural whys.
intro.cn: why 是不带任何词缀的疑问词，它唯一的派生形式是复数 whys。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin source; the Latin entries below show the borrowed relatives such as quare and causa.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目展示 quare、causa 这类借入的相关词。

items.example: It works as adverb and noun.
It softens advice into a question.

items.exampleCN: 这里疑问词变成关系词。

items.example: It carries where plus for, not why.
items.exampleCN: 它由 where 与 for 组成，并非来自 why。

items.example: It adds a tone of disbelief.
items.exampleCN: 它增添难以置信的语气。

items.example: It answers a why with a shrug.
items.exampleCN: 它用一个耸肩回答「为什么」。

latinEntries.example: It is the closest Latin question of cause.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语中最接近的原因问词。

latinEntries.example: It gives the English cause.

definition_zh: 邪恶的；恶劣的；淘气的；极好的（口语）
definition_en: morally bad and cruel, and in informal use playfully naughty or even excellent
core_image: 童话里披黑斗篷的巫婆，指尖亮着一点绿火，嘴角歪着笑
scene: 童话书里那个披黑斗篷的人把药水滴进杯子，嘴角一直歪着笑，孩子们都屏住了呼吸。The wicked queen offered the girl a shining red apple.
sceneCN: 这里 wicked 是「邪恶的」（第 1 个义项：在道德上坏且残忍）；句意为那个邪恶的王后递给女孩一只发亮的红苹果。黑斗篷、绿火与歪着的笑，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Morally bad
senses.definition: evil in intention or action, deliberately doing harm to others
senses.definitionCN: 在意图或行为上为恶，有意伤害他人
senses.example: The wicked queen offered the girl a shining red apple.
senses.exampleCN: 那个邪恶的王后递给女孩一只发亮的红苹果。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply bad and evil, the moral judgement a community passes on a person.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是坏、恶，是群体对一个人做出的道德判断。

senses.title: Cruel in a smaller way
senses.definition: used of words, weather or tricks that are harsh and deliberately unkind
senses.definitionCN: 形容言辞、天气或恶作剧暴烈而存心不善
senses.example: It was a wicked trick to hide his shoes before the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前把他的鞋藏起来，这恶作剧够坏的。
senses.why: The moral word stretched to anything that causes needless pain, not only to people.
senses.whyCN: 这个道德词扩展到一切造成不必要痛苦的事物，不再只指人。

senses.title: Playfully naughty
senses.definition: used of children or humour that is mischievous but not truly bad
senses.definitionCN: 形容孩子或幽默带点顽皮，但并不真的坏
senses.example: She gave me a wicked little smile and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她冲我调皮地笑了笑，什么也没说。
senses.why: With a child or a joke the danger is only pretended, so the harsh word turns affectionate.
senses.whyCN: 用在孩子或玩笑上时，危险只是假装出来的，严厉的词于是变得亲昵。

senses.title: Excellent, in slang
senses.definition: in modern informal speech, used to praise something as very good or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 在现代口语中，用来称赞某事极好、令人赞叹
senses.example: He plays a wicked guitar solo in the last verse.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一段弹了一段绝妙的吉他独奏。
senses.why: Slang often flips a bad word into praise, because the intensity of the judgement stays and only its sign changes.
senses.whyCN: 俚语常把贬词翻成褒词，因为判断的强度仍在，只是方向反了。

intro.en: Wicked comes from Middle English wikked, from wicke, meaning evil or bewitched, which is linked to wicca, a witch.
intro.cn: wicked 来自中古英语 wikked，源头 wicke 意为「邪恶的、被施了妖术的」，与 wicca（女巫）相关。

items.en: The root wicce meant a female magician, and the related adjective carried the sense of bewitched.
items.cn: 词根 wicce 指女巫，相关形容词带有「被施了妖术」之意。

items.en: Wikked described a person who was evil or given to the dark arts, and the -ed ending marked the adjective.
items.cn: wikked 描述行恶或习于邪术的人，-ed 词尾标示形容词。

items.en: The ending lost its separate force, and the word became the plain adjective for moral evil.
items.cn: 该词尾失去了独立作用，这个词成为表示道德恶的普通形容词。

items.en: With children and jokes it softened into playful naughtiness, as in a wicked grin.
items.cn: 用在孩子和玩笑上时，它软化为顽皮的淘气，如 a wicked grin。

items.en: Modern slang turned it into high praise, so a wicked solo is a fine one.
items.cn: 现代俚语把它变成高度称赞，所以 a wicked solo 指的是一段漂亮独奏。

note.en: The first group gathers witch-family words that look or sound similar, the second the words for evil and for mischief.
note.cn: 第一组收与 witch 同族或形近的词，第二组收表示邪恶与淘气的词。

entries.definition: A woman said to work magic, behind the old adjective.
The string in a candle that feeds the flame.
Woven from thin branches, quite unrelated.
The quality of being wicked.
Morally bad in a deep and serious way.
Willing to cause pain without pity.
Bad in a small and childish way.

normalIntro.en: Wicked carries the old word for a witch, so the fairy-tale picture is the shortest road into it.
normalIntro.cn: wicked 里藏着古老的「女巫」一词，所以童话画面是通往它最近的路。

normal.en: Witch hides inside wicked; a witch was once called wicce.
normal.cn: wicked 里藏着 witch，而女巫曾被叫作 wicce。

normal.en: The -ed only made it an adjective, like crooked from crook.
normal.cn: 这个 -ed 只是把它变成形容词，像 crooked 来自 crook。

normal.en: A wicked stepmother and a wicked smile differ only in how dangerous they are.
normal.cn: 恶毒的后母与调皮的一笑，区别只在于危险程度。

normal.en: Modern slang flips it: a wicked solo is great, not evil.
normal.cn: 现代俚语把它翻转：a wicked solo 是好，不是坏。

normal.en: No peace for the wicked is a joke said while working late.
normal.cn: no peace for the wicked 是加班时的自嘲。

abstract.en: See a black cloak and one hand raised in the dark.
abstract.cn: 看见一件黑斗篷和黑暗中举起的一只手。

abstract.en: Feel the room go quiet when a certain smile appears.
abstract.cn: 感觉某个笑容一出现，房间里就安静下来。

abstract.en: Hear laughter that is too pleased with itself.
abstract.cn: 听见一阵对自己太满意的笑。

examples.en: In the story a wicked giant guards the bridge.
examples.cn: 故事里有个邪恶的巨人守着那座桥。

examples.en: That was a wicked thing to say to your brother.
examples.cn: 对弟弟说那种话可真恶毒。

examples.en: She has a wicked sense of humour that keeps us laughing.
examples.cn: 她的幽默感刁钻得很，总让我们发笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克的」——维克这个人在故事里总干坏事，所以是邪恶的。

root: 古英语 wicce（女巫）→ 中古英语 wicke（邪恶）→ wikked → 现代英语 wicked；同族有 witch、wickedness、wickedly。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a moral judgement tied to witchcraft, widens to harsh words and weather, softens towards a child s mischief, and in slang flips into praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词最初是与巫术相关的道德判断，扩展到严厉的言辞与天气，再软化为孩子的顽皮，最后在俚语中翻成称赞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black cloak, green fire on a fingertip, a crooked smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑斗篷、指尖的绿火与歪着的笑。

branches.en: The fairy-tale branch: the queen and the red apple.
branches.cn: 童话分支：王后与那只红苹果。

branches.en: The trick branch: shoes hidden before a race.
branches.cn: 恶作剧分支：赛前被藏起来的鞋。

branches.en: The affection branch: a small, wicked smile.
branches.cn: 亲昵分支：调皮的一笑。

branches.en: The praise branch: a wicked guitar solo.
branches.cn: 称赞分支：一段绝妙的吉他独奏。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a verdict on a person or a deed.
branches.cn: 评判分支：对人或行为的裁决。

intro.en: Wicked is an old adjective formed with the ending -ed on a stem meaning evil, and it now builds adverbs and nouns with -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: wicked 是在表示邪恶的词干上加 -ed 构成的古老形容词，现在还可用 -ly、-ness 派生副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show the borrowed words that translate it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目给出用来翻译它的借入词。

items.example: It turned the old noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把古老的名词变成形容词。

items.example: It is the oldest shape behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词背后最古老的形态。

items.example: It kept the stem without the ending.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了没有词尾的词干。

items.example: A separate word from the same family sound.
items.exampleCN: 同族中一个形似的独立词。

items.meaning: the cruel figure of fairy tales
items.example: The fixed frame of the old sense.

latinEntries.example: It gives English malice and malignant.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出英语的 malice 与 malignant。

latinEntries.example: It gives English nefarious.

definition_zh: 宽的；宽阔的；广泛的；睁大的；差得远的
definition_en: measuring a large distance from one side to the other, and figuratively covering a large range
core_image: 一条从田埂这头一直铺到那头的大河，两岸之间没有桥，只有很宽很宽的河面
scene: 站在河堤上，对岸的树像一条细线，中间的水面宽得望不到边。The river is so wide that the other bank looks like a thin grey line.
sceneCN: 这里 wide 是「宽的」（第 1 个义项：从一边到另一边距离大）；句意为河那么宽，对岸看起来像一条灰细线。那条铺满整个视野、中间没有桥的河面，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 宽的；宽阔的；广泛的；睁大的

senses.title: Large from side to side
senses.definition: measuring a good distance from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从一边到另一边有相当长的距离
senses.example: The river is so wide that the other bank looks like a thin grey line.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河那么宽，对岸看起来像一条灰细线。
senses.why: This physical span is the oldest and most literal sense, and every other use grows from it.
senses.whyCN: 这种物理上的跨度是最古老、最字面的意思，其他用法都从它长出来。

senses.title: Covering a large range
senses.definition: including many different things, kinds or people
senses.definitionCN: 包括许多不同的事物、种类或人
senses.example: The shop sells a wide range of tools and paints.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售种类广泛的工具和油漆。
senses.why: A wide spread covers much ground, and a list of many kinds spreads in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 宽阔的摊开占据大片地面，而涵盖许多种类的清单也是以同样方式铺开的。

senses.title: Fully open
senses.definition: used of eyes or doors that are opened to the full
senses.definitionCN: 形容眼睛或门被完全打开
senses.example: She stared at the letter with wide eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她睁大眼睛盯着那封信。
senses.why: A fully opened eye is stretched from side to side, so the measurement becomes a state of opening.
senses.whyCN: 完全睁开的眼睛两边拉长，于是这种度量变成了一种打开的状态。

senses.title: Far from the target
senses.definition: used of an answer or a shot that misses by a large distance
senses.definitionCN: 形容答案或射击偏离目标很远
senses.example: His guess was wide of the mark and made everyone laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 他猜得完全不对，把大家都逗笑了。
senses.why: An arrow landing wide of the target is simply far across the field, and the image carried over to answers.
senses.whyCN: 箭落在靶子旁边的宽处，不过是横过大片场地，这一形象又被带到了答案上。

senses.title: Completely, in adverb use
senses.definition: as an adverb, used with open or apart to mean to the full extent
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时与 open、apart 搭配，表示达到最大限度
senses.example: The windows stood wide open all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午窗子都大开着。
senses.why: The adjective took the adverb job because English wants a word that measures the full opening.
senses.whyCN: 形容词承担了副词的工作，因为英语需要一个词来衡量完全打开的程度。

intro.en: Wide comes from Old English wid, from a Germanic root that also gives width, and its first meaning was simply broad.
intro.cn: wide 源自古英语 wid，其日耳曼语词根也给出 width，最初的意思就是「宽阔」。

items.en: The root described something spread out across space, as opposed to long from end to end.
items.cn: 这个词根描述的是一样东西在空间中横向铺开，与「从头到尾的长」相对。

items.en: Wid meant broad and spacious, and the noun widu was already forming beside it.
items.cn: wid 表示宽阔、空旷，旁边已经出现了名词形式。

items.en: The spelling became wide, and the word began to describe range as well as width.
items.cn: 拼写变为 wide，这个词除了宽度也开始描述范围。

items.en: Expressions such as a wide range and wide open extended it from the physical to the abstract.
items.cn: a wide range、wide open 这类说法把它从物理延伸到抽象。

items.en: The adverb use survives mainly in set pairs such as wide open, wide apart and far and wide.
items.cn: 副词用法主要保存在 wide open、wide apart、far and wide 等固定搭配中。

note.en: The first group gathers the other words of measurement, the second the words for a large range or spread.
note.cn: 第一组收其他度量词，第二组收表示范围大、分布广的词。

entries.definition: The measurement itself, from side to side.
To make or become wide.
Living free in nature, a different word.
Measuring a large distance end to end, the other axis.
Wide, often of shoulders, roads or views.
Covering a large area or range.
Extremely wide, almost beyond measuring.

normalIntro.en: Wide is a measurement word, so picture something you could run across rather than turn end for end.
normalIntro.cn: wide 是度量词，所以要想象一样能横着跑过去的东西，而不是把它转一整圈。

normal.en: Wide and long are two axes; a door is wide, and a corridor is long.
normal.cn: wide 与 long 是两条轴：门是宽的，走廊是长的。

normal.en: Wide eyes and wide open share one picture of stretching to the limit.
normal.cn: wide eyes 与 wide open 共用一幅拉到极限的画面。

normal.en: A wide range is the same stretch, filled with kinds instead of metres.
normal.cn: a wide range 是同一种铺开，只是填的不是米，而是种类。

normal.en: Width turns the adjective into a noun by adding th.
normal.cn: width 加 th 就把形容词变成了名词。

normal.en: Far and wide means the span of the whole map.
normal.cn: far and wide 就是整张地图那么大的跨度。

abstract.en: Feel the wind crossing an open valley with nothing to stop it.
abstract.cn: 感觉风横穿开阔山谷，没有任何东西挡它。

abstract.en: See two banks so far apart that a voice would not carry.
abstract.cn: 看见两岸远到喊一声都传不过去。

abstract.en: Feel your eyes stretching at a surprising line.
abstract.cn: 感觉眼睛被一句意外的话撑开。

examples.en: The road is wide enough for two trucks to pass.
examples.cn: 这条路宽得能并排过两辆卡车。

examples.en: The museum offers a wide choice of free tours.
examples.cn: 博物馆提供了种类丰富的免费导览。

examples.en: She left the door wide open behind her.
examples.cn: 她离开时把门大开着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外得」——外面得留出很宽的余地，所以是宽的。

root: 日耳曼语词根（横向铺开）→ 古英语 wid（宽阔）→ 中古英语 wide → 现代英语 wide；同族有 width、widen、widely、widespread。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with the physical span from side to side, spreads to a range of things, to eyes opened fully, to a shot missing by a distance, and finally to the adverbial fully.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从左右之间的物理跨度出发，扩展到事物的范围、睁大的眼睛、偏得很远的射击，最后成为表示「完全」的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river so broad that the far bank is only a thin line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条大河宽到对岸只剩一条细线。

branches.en: The river branch: two banks far apart.
branches.cn: 河流分支：两岸相距很远。

branches.en: The range branch: tools and paints of many kinds.
branches.cn: 范围分支：种类繁多的工具与油漆。

branches.en: The eyes branch: staring at a letter.
branches.cn: 眼睛分支：盯着那封信。

branches.en: The miss branch: a guess wide of the mark.
branches.cn: 偏离分支：猜得完全不对。

branches.en: The adverb branch: windows wide open.
branches.cn: 副词分支：窗子大开着。

intro.en: Wide is a free Germanic adjective that builds the noun width, the verb widen and the adverbs widely and wide.
intro.cn: wide 是自由使用的日耳曼语形容词，可派生名词 width、动词 widen 以及副词 widely、wide。

latinIntro.en: The native word has no Latin source; the Latin entries below give the borrowed words often used for breadth and range.
latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出常用来表达宽度与范围的借入词。

items.example: It works as adjective and adverb.

items.meaning: in a way, over a range

items.example: The adverb keeps its old breadth.
items.exampleCN: 副词保留了旧日的宽度感。

items.example: The pair spreads the word in two directions.
items.exampleCN: 这一对词把跨度向两个方向拉开。

items.example: It comes from shooting at a mark.

latinEntries.example: It gives English latitude, first width then freedom.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出 latitude，先指宽度后指自由。

latinEntries.example: It gives English ample.

definition_zh: 广泛地；普遍地；大大地；相隔很远地
definition_en: over a large area or among many people, and also by a large amount
core_image: 一张地图上密密麻麻插满了小旗，旗子从最东边一直排到最西边
scene: 墙上挂着世界地图，同一种小旗从东边一路插到西边，几乎每个国家都有一面。The method is now widely used in hospitals across the country.
sceneCN: 这里 widely 是「广泛地」（第 1 个义项：在大范围内或许多人中间）；句意为这种方法如今在全国各地的医院里广泛使用。地图上从东到西插满小旗，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: In many places
senses.definition: in a large number of places or among a large number of people
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方或许多人中间
senses.example: The method is now widely used in hospitals across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方法如今在全国各地的医院里广泛使用。
senses.why: The adverb simply says that the adjective spreads over a large area of use.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是说明形容词所指的范围铺展到了很大的使用面上。

senses.title: By a large amount
senses.definition: by a large degree or difference, often before words such as different or vary
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上或差距上很大，常放在 different、vary 之前
senses.example: Prices vary widely between the two cities.
senses.exampleCN: 两个城市的价格差别很大。
senses.why: Here the width is in the difference rather than in space, and the gap itself is broad.
senses.whyCN: 这里的宽度在于差距而不在于空间，拉开的是差距本身。

senses.title: Over long distances
senses.definition: used of two things placed far apart from each other
senses.definitionCN: 形容两个事物彼此相距很远
senses.example: The two villages are widely separated by the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个村子被沼泽隔得很远。
senses.why: The physical sense stays intact when the adverb measures the gap between two points.
senses.whyCN: 当副词度量两点间的间隔时，物理意义仍然完好。

senses.title: To travel extensively
senses.definition: used with verbs such as travel or read to mean over a very large extent
senses.definitionCN: 与 travel、read 等动词连用，表示范围极广
senses.example: He has travelled widely in Asia and still keeps a diary.
senses.exampleCN: 他在亚洲游历甚广，至今仍写日记。
senses.why: Movement across a wide map was the first use of the word, and it is still the easiest to picture.
senses.whyCN: 横越大片地图的移动是这个词最早的用法，至今也是最容易想象的。

intro.en: Widely is wide plus the adverb ending -ly, and it appeared once wide had already acquired the sense of a range.
intro.cn: widely 是 wide 加副词词尾 -ly，产生于 wide 已具备「范围」之义之后。

items.en: Wid meant broad, and the adverb widlice meant over a wide space.
items.cn: wid 表示宽阔，副词 widlice 表示在宽阔的范围内。

items.en: The form shifted to widely, and it began to appear with verbs of spreading and travelling.
items.cn: 词形移向 widely，开始与传播、旅行一类动词连用。

items.en: With travel and reading it described a person of broad experience.
items.cn: 与 travel、read 连用时，它描述阅历广的人。

items.en: Technology and commerce gave it the fixed company of used, known and available.
items.cn: 科技与商业让它与 used、known、available 固定搭配。

items.en: Before words such as different and vary it came to mean by a large degree.
items.cn: 放在 different、vary 等词前，它就表示「在很大程度」。

note.en: The first group gathers other -ly adverbs that look similar, the second the words that stress breadth of use.
note.cn: 第一组收形近的其他 -ly 副词，第二组收强调使用广泛的词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb.
The noun of measurement.
The verb of making broader.
Cunning, with one letter fewer.
In most cases or among most people.
Over a large area or in great detail.
By many ordinary people.

normalIntro.en: Widely is the adverb of spread, so its best pictures are maps and crowds rather than measures.
normalIntro.cn: widely 是「铺开」的副词，所以它最好的画面是地图和人群，而不是尺子。

normal.en: Wide plus ly: the adjective becomes a way of happening.
normal.cn: wide 加 ly：形容词变成了一种发生的方式。

normal.en: Widely used and widely known are the two commonest pairs.
normal.cn: widely used 与 widely known 是最常见的两对搭配。

normal.en: Vary widely puts the width into the difference, not the map.
normal.cn: vary widely 把宽度放进了差别里，而不是地图上。

normal.en: Read widely means the books are spread out, not thick.
normal.cn: read widely 说明书读得广，而不是读得厚。

normal.en: Widely separated is the only one that keeps the old physical sense.
normal.cn: widely separated 是唯一保留古老物理意义的搭配。

abstract.en: See flags pushed into a map from edge to edge.
abstract.cn: 看见小旗从地图一边插到另一边。

abstract.en: Hear one word repeated in a hundred mouths.
abstract.cn: 听见一个词在一百张嘴中重复。

abstract.en: Feel a habit spread through a whole city in a season.
abstract.cn: 感觉一种习惯在一个季节里传遍整座城。

examples.en: The new vaccine is widely available in rural areas.
examples.cn: 这种新疫苗在农村地区也能广泛获得。

examples.en: Opinions on the plan differ widely among the staff.
examples.cn: 员工对这个计划的看法差别很大。

examples.en: She read widely before writing her first novel.
examples.cn: 写第一部小说之前，她读了大量书籍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外的里」——从外面一直铺到里面，处处都有，就是广泛地。

root: 古英语 wid（宽阔）+ 副词词尾 -ly → 中古英语 widely → 现代英语 widely；同族有 wide、widen、widespread。

sensesIntro.en: The word says that something reaches many places, then measures a large difference, then the distance between two points, and finally the breadth of a person s travel.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先说明某事到达许多地方，接着度量很大的差别，然后是两点之间的距离，最后是个人游历的广度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flags pushed into a world map from one edge to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面面小旗从地图的一边插到另一边。

branches.en: The spread branch: a method used in many hospitals.
branches.cn: 传播分支：许多医院都在用的方法。

branches.en: The difference branch: prices that vary widely.
branches.cn: 差别分支：价格相差很大。

branches.en: The distance branch: two villages far apart.
branches.cn: 距离分支：相隔很远的两个村子。

branches.en: The travel branch: a man who has travelled widely.
branches.cn: 游历分支：游历甚广的人。

branches.en: The degree branch: the same word for space and for amount.
branches.cn: 程度分支：空间与数量共用同一个词。

intro.en: Widely is a plain -ly adverb on wide, so its structure is the whole point: the suffix turns a measure into a manner.
intro.cn: widely 是加在 wide 上的普通 -ly 副词，它的结构就是全部要点：后缀把度量变成了方式。

latinIntro.en: The base is native Germanic, so there is no Latin source; the Latin entries below give the closest borrowed adverbs.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出最接近的借入副词。

items.example: Here the width is a gap.

latinEntries.example: It gives English latitude through the adjective.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它经由形容词给出英语的 latitude。

definition_zh: 加宽；拓宽；扩大；（差距）拉大；睁大
definition_en: to make something broader, or to become broader, and figuratively to increase a range or a gap
core_image: 一条原本只容一人通过的小路，被两边的铁锹一点点挖宽
scene: 工人们沿着小路两侧挖土，把路面一点点加宽，好让手推车也能过去。They plan to widen the road before the summer holidays.
sceneCN: 这里 widen 是「加宽」（第 1 个义项：使某物从一边到另一边的距离变大）；句意为他们打算在暑假前把这条路加宽。两把铁锹把窄路一点点挖宽，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 加宽；拓宽；扩大；变得更大

senses.title: To make physically broader
senses.definition: to increase the width of a road, a hole or a passage
senses.definitionCN: 增大道路、洞口或通道的宽度
senses.example: They plan to widen the road before the summer holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打算在暑假前把这条路加宽。
senses.why: The verb simply puts the adjective into action on a piece of ground or stone.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词只是把形容词的宽度落实到一段地面或石块上。

senses.title: To become broader
senses.definition: to grow wider by itself, without anyone making it happen
senses.definitionCN: 自身变宽变大，并非由人推动
senses.example: The river widens as it reaches the plain.
senses.exampleCN: 河流到了平原就变宽了。
senses.why: English often uses the same verb for doing and for happening, and here the road does it to itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让同一个动词兼顾「做」与「发生」，这里路自己变宽了。

senses.title: To enlarge a range
senses.definition: to make a set of things, people or chances larger
senses.definitionCN: 使事物、人物或机会的集合变大
senses.example: Reading in two languages will widen your experience.
senses.exampleCN: 用两种语言阅读会拓宽你的阅历。
senses.why: A wider field holds more, so stretching a range is the same motion applied to ideas.
senses.whyCN: 更宽的场地能容纳更多，所以扩大范围就是把同一个动作用在想法上。

senses.title: To increase a gap
senses.definition: used of a distance or difference between two sides that grows larger
senses.definitionCN: 指两方之间的距离或差别变得更大
senses.example: The gap between the two teams widened after the second goal.
senses.exampleCN: 第二个球之后，两队之间的差距拉大了。
senses.why: The space between two points is stretched in the same way as a road, only nobody digs it.
senses.whyCN: 两点之间的空间被拉宽，和修路是一个动作，只是没人动手挖。

senses.title: Eyes growing round
senses.definition: used of eyes that open wider through surprise or fear
senses.definitionCN: 形容眼睛因惊讶或恐惧而睁得更大
senses.example: Her eyes widened when she heard the price.
senses.exampleCN: 听到价格时，她的眼睛睁大了。
senses.why: The eye opens sideways like a small road, and the same verb covers that move.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛像一条小路那样向两边打开，同一个动词也就覆盖了这个动作。

intro.en: Widen is a native verb built by adding the Old English ending -en to wid, broad, the same pattern that produced deepen and strengthen.
intro.cn: widen 是在「宽阔」的 wid 上加古英语词尾 -en 构成的本土动词，与 deepen、strengthen 是同一模式。

items.en: The ending -en turned adjectives into verbs meaning to make that quality, as in hwit becoming hwitnian.
items.cn: 词尾 -en 把形容词变成表示「使之具有该性质」的动词，如 hwit 变成 hwitnian。

items.en: Widnen appears in writing for making something broader, still close to its physical sense.
items.cn: 中古英语中 widnen 已用于表示加宽，仍贴近物理意义。

items.en: The spelling settled as widen, and the word spread from roads to ranges and to gaps.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 widen，这个词从道路扩展到范围与差距。

items.en: Abstract uses such as widen your experience became common in writing about education.
items.cn: widen your experience 一类抽象用法在教育写作中变得常见。

items.en: The eye-filling phrase eyes widened became a fixed image of surprise in modern prose.
items.cn: eyes widened 这一说法在现代散文里成了表示惊讶的固定形象。

note.en: The first group gathers the other -en verbs of the same kind, the second the verbs of making something larger.
note.cn: 第一组收同类的其他 -en 动词，第二组收表示扩大的动词。

entries.definition: To make or become deep.
To make or become strong.
The noun beside the verb.
The adjective the verb comes from.
To make broader, often of experience or outlook.
To grow larger in all directions.
To make longer or to reach further.

normalIntro.en: Widen is an -en verb, so its shape is simply the adjective with a verb ending attached.
normalIntro.cn: widen 是个 -en 动词，它的形状就是形容词后面接上一个动词词尾。

normal.en: Deep, strength and wide all take -en to become actions.
normal.cn: deep、strength、wide 都加 -en 变成动作。

normal.en: A road is widened with spades, a river widens on its own.
normal.cn: 路要靠铁锹加宽，河却自己变宽。

normal.en: Widen a gap and nobody digs, the distance just grows.
normal.cn: 拉大差距时没人动土，距离自己长大。

normal.en: Read two languages and your experience widens.
normal.cn: 读两种语言，阅历就拓宽了。

normal.en: Eyes widen before the mouth has time to speak.
normal.cn: 眼睛先睁大，嘴还没来得及说话。

abstract.en: See a narrow path slowly breathing outwards.
abstract.cn: 看见一条小路慢慢向两边舒展开。

abstract.en: Feel the two banks of a river step apart.
abstract.cn: 感觉河的两岸一步步让开。

abstract.en: Hear a range of choices grow until it reaches the wall.
abstract.cn: 听一个选择范围一直长到墙边。

examples.en: The council agreed to widen the bridge next spring.
examples.cn: 议会同意明年春天拓宽这座桥。

examples.en: The gap between rich and poor has widened again.
examples.cn: 贫富差距又一次拉大了。

examples.en: His eyes widened when the door opened by itself.
examples.cn: 门自己打开时，他的眼睛睁大了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外的恩」——外面又得恩赐一块地，所以路宽了。

root: 古英语 wid（宽阔）+ 动词词尾 -en → 中古英语 widnen → 现代英语 widen；同族有 wide、width、widely。

sensesIntro.en: The verb makes a road broader, lets a river broaden itself, stretches a range of choices, opens a growing gap, and finally opens a pair of eyes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词把路加宽，让河自己变宽，拉开选择的范围，张开越变越大的差距，最后睁大一双眼睛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two spades cutting a narrow path wider.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把铁锹把窄路一点点挖宽。

branches.en: The road branch: widening before the holidays.
branches.cn: 道路分支：假期前动工加宽。

branches.en: The river branch: the water spreading on the plain.
branches.cn: 河流分支：水在平原上散开。

branches.en: The experience branch: reading in two languages.
branches.cn: 阅历分支：用两种语言阅读。

branches.en: The gap branch: two teams drawing apart.
branches.cn: 差距分支：两支队伍越拉越远。

branches.en: The surprise branch: eyes opening at a price.
branches.cn: 惊讶分支：听到价格时睁大的眼睛。

intro.en: Widen is a good example of a productive suffix: -en on an adjective makes a verb meaning to make or become that way.
intro.cn: widen 是能产后缀的好例子：-en 加在形容词上，造出「使…或变得…」的动词。

latinIntro.en: The base is native, but the same job is done in Latin by the suffix -are on adjectives; the entries below show borrowed verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是本土的，而拉丁语中由形容词加 -are 完成同样的工作；下面的条目展示借入的动词。

items.example: The abstract use of the verb.
A common frame in news writing.
items.exampleCN: 新闻写作中的常见框架。

latinEntries.example: It lies behind the English amplify.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是英语 amplify 的来源。
