definition_zh: 普遍的；广泛的；分布广的；广为流传的
definition_en: found or happening in many places or among many people over a large area
core_image: 一张大地图上，同一种颜色的斑点从一角蔓到另一角
scene: 地图上同一颜色的斑点从海边一路爬到山那边，几乎没有空白的地方。There is widespread support for the new library among local families.
sceneCN: 这里 widespread 是「普遍的」（第 1 个义项：在许多地方或许多人中都能见到）；句意为当地家庭普遍支持新建图书馆。地图上从一角蔓到另一角的同色斑点，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 普遍的；分布广的；广为流传的

senses.title: Found in many places
senses.definition: existing in many places over an area, as a plant, a habit or a problem
senses.definitionCN: 在一片区域内许多地方都存在，如植物、习惯或问题
senses.example: There is widespread support for the new library among local families.
senses.exampleCN: 当地家庭普遍支持新建图书馆。
senses.why: The compound is literally spread wide, so the picture is a thing lying across a whole region.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词字面就是「铺得很宽」，画面是一件横卧在整个区域上的东西。

senses.title: Happening to many people
senses.definition: used of events, damage or illness that affect a large share of people
senses.definitionCN: 形容事件、破坏或疾病影响很大一部分人
senses.example: The storm caused widespread damage along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴给沿海带来大面积破坏。
senses.why: A storm does not choose one house, and the adjective marks damage that reaches everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 风暴不会只挑一栋房子，这个形容词标记的正是什么都波及到的损坏。

senses.title: Believed by many people
senses.definition: used of ideas, beliefs or reports that are held by a great many people
senses.definitionCN: 形容被众多人持有的观念、看法或报道
senses.example: It is a widespread belief that owls can see in total darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 人们普遍认为猫头鹰能在全黑的夜里看见东西。
senses.why: An idea spreads like a seed across a field, so the same compound covers opinion.
senses.whyCN: 想法像种子一样撒满田野，于是同一个复合词也覆盖了意见。

senses.title: In general commercial use
senses.definition: used of a product, tool or method that has reached a large share of the market
senses.definitionCN: 形容产品或方法已进入大部分市场
senses.example: The technology became widespread only after the price fell.
senses.exampleCN: 这项技术直到价格下降后才被广泛使用。
senses.why: The word measures reach rather than depth, so it suits goods that are everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量的是覆盖而不深度，因此适用于到处都是的东西。

intro.en: Widespread is a clear modern compound of wide and the past participle spread, literally spread over a wide area.
intro.cn: widespread 是 wide 与过去分词 spread 的现代复合词，字面就是「铺得很宽」。

items.en: Wid meant broad, and spraedan meant to stretch out or scatter.
items.cn: wid 表示宽阔，spraedan 表示铺开、撒开。

items.en: The participle spred described a cloth or a rumour laid out over a surface.
items.cn: 分词 spred 描述铺在表面上的布或传开的谣言。

items.en: The two parts joined in the eighteenth century to describe things reaching across a region.
items.cn: 两部分在十八世纪合起来，用来描述横跨一片区域的事物。

items.en: Reporting of disease and weather made it a favourite word for damage and infection.
items.cn: 对疾病与天气的报道使它成为形容破坏与感染的爱用词。

items.en: It now also covers beliefs and technology, anything whose reach is the point.
items.cn: 如今它也覆盖信念与技术，凡是以「覆盖广度」为要点的事物都可使用。

note.en: The first group gathers compounds built on spread or wide, the second the words for general extent.
note.cn: 第一组收以 spread 或 wide 构成的复合词，第二组收表示普遍程度的词。

entries.definition: To stretch out or scatter over an area.
Having effects over a wide area, a close cousin.
The measuring element inside the compound.
Having read a lot, another hyphen-free compound.
Found often, in many places.
Affecting nearly all, not special.
True of everyone everywhere.

normalIntro.en: Widespread is easy to spell and easy to picture: take spread and put wide in front of it.
normalIntro.cn: widespread 既好拼又好想：把 spread 铺开，前面加个 wide。

normal.en: Spread is already flat, and wide makes it reach the edges.
normal.cn: spread 已经是平的，wide 让它一直铺到边上。

normal.en: The compound never changes form, so no comparison is needed.
normal.cn: 这个复合词形式不变，所以也不需要比较级。

normal.en: Damage, support and belief all lie across the same wide map.
normal.cn: 破坏、支持与信念都躺在同一张宽地图上。

normal.en: A rumour becomes widespread faster than a fact.
normal.cn: 谣言比事实更容易变得人人皆知。

normal.en: Widespread use means the tool is in every kitchen.
normal.cn: widespread use 说明这工具家家都有。

abstract.en: See one colour creep across a whole map.
abstract.cn: 看见一种颜色在大地图上慢慢爬开。

abstract.en: Feel a belief repeated in every shop you pass.
abstract.cn: 感觉每经过一家店都听见同一个看法。

abstract.en: Hear a whisper grow into a general roar.
abstract.cn: 听一句耳语长成一片轰鸣。

examples.en: There was widespread criticism of the decision.
examples.cn: 这个决定受到了广泛批评。

examples.en: Flooding caused widespread damage to the rice fields.
examples.cn: 洪水给稻田造成大面积破坏。

examples.en: Mobile payment is now widespread even in small towns.
examples.cn: 如今连小城镇也普遍使用移动支付。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外的斯普瑞德」——外边到处都铺开了，所以很普遍。

root: wide（宽阔）+ spread（铺开）→ 十八世纪复合为 widespread；同族有 wide、widely、spread。

sensesIntro.en: The compound describes support that reaches many families, damage that covers a coast, a belief held by many, and a tool that is everywhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个复合词描述遍及许多家庭的支持、覆盖整条海岸的破坏、众人持有的看法，以及到处都在用的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one colour of dots creeping from one corner of a map to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一种颜色的斑点从地图一角爬到另一角。

branches.en: The support branch: families behind the new library.
branches.cn: 支持分支：支持新图书馆的众多家庭。

branches.en: The storm branch: damage along the whole coast.
branches.cn: 风暴分支：整条海岸的破坏。

branches.en: The belief branch: owls and the darkest night.
branches.cn: 看法分支：猫头鹰与最黑的夜。

branches.en: The market branch: a technology after the price fell.
branches.cn: 市场分支：降价后的技术。

branches.en: The reach branch: measuring breadth, not depth.
branches.cn: 覆盖分支：量的是广度，不是深度。

intro.en: Widespread is a transparent compound of two free words, and the first element wide does the whole job of measuring breadth.
intro.cn: widespread 是两个自由词构成的透明复合词，第一个成分 wide 承担了全部度量广度的任务。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native Germanic, so there is no Latin source; the Latin entries below give the borrowed equivalents.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出借入的对应词。

items.exampleCN: 副词工作由 widely 承担。

latinEntries.example: It gives English vulgar in its old sense.
It gives English diffuse.

definition_zh: 寡妇；遗孀；使成为寡妇；独占（口语）
definition_en: a woman whose husband has died and who has not married again, and the verb of making her so
core_image: 一间只摆着一把椅子的空屋，窗台上还放着两个人的照片
scene: 村里那位老妇人自从丈夫走后，就一直一个人守着院子里那把旧椅子。The widow next door still keeps two chairs on her porch.
sceneCN: 这里 widow 是「寡妇」（第 1 个义项：丈夫去世后没有再婚的妇女）；句意为隔壁的寡妇仍在门廊上放着两把椅子。只摆一把椅子的空屋，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A woman whose husband died
senses.definition: a woman who has lost her husband by death and has not married again
senses.definitionCN: 丈夫去世后没有再婚的妇女
senses.example: The widow next door still keeps two chairs on her porch.
senses.exampleCN: 隔壁的寡妇仍在门廊上放着两把椅子。
senses.why: The noun is one of the oldest words for a person left alone by death, and it has almost no figurative life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是最古老的、指因死亡而独留一人的名词之一，几乎不带比喻用法。

senses.title: The male counterpart
senses.definition: used in the phrase widow and widower, the pair naming the two sides of the same loss
senses.definitionCN: 用于 widow and widower 这一对照说法，指同一损失的男女两面
senses.example: The law then spoke of widows but said nothing of widowers.
senses.exampleCN: 那时的法律只提到寡妇，对鳏夫只字未提。
senses.why: The newer form widower was made by adding -er to match other pairs such as speaker and listener.
senses.whyCN: 较晚出现的 widower 是加 -er 造出来的，以与 speaker、listener 等成对词语对齐。

senses.title: To make someone a widow
senses.definition: in older or formal use, to take away a person s partner by death
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或正式用法，指因死亡而使某人失去配偶
senses.example: War widowed thousands of women in a single decade.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间，战争使成千上万的女性成为寡妇。
senses.why: A noun became a verb because English likes to turn a state into an act.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了动词，因为英语喜欢把状态转写成动作。

senses.title: A short last line of a paragraph
senses.definition: in printing, a single short line at the top of a page left from the previous paragraph
senses.definitionCN: 印刷排版中，上一段遗留在页面顶部的一行孤零零的文字
senses.example: The editor closed the widow at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把页首那行孤立的字收了回来。
senses.why: A printers term borrowed it because the line stands alone at the top of a page, like someone left behind.
senses.whyCN: 印刷术语借用了这个词，因为那行字孤零零立在页顶，像被留下的人。

senses.title: In card games and informal use
senses.definition: in card games, an extra hand dealt to players, and in casual speech to be left without a partner
senses.definitionCN: 牌戏中指额外补发的手牌，口语中指被撇下没有搭档
senses.example: We were three, so one player had to sit out as the widow.
senses.exampleCN: 我们是三个人，只好让一位当没搭档的那个。
senses.why: The metaphor of being left alone travelled into games and into jokes about odd numbers.
senses.whyCN: 「被留下」的比喻进入了牌戏，也进入了关于人数的玩笑。

intro.en: Widow descends from Old English widewe, from a Germanic root meaning empty or separated, related to the Latin vidua.
intro.cn: widow 源自古英语 widewe，其日耳曼语词根意为「空的、被分开的」，与拉丁语 vidua 同源。

items.en: The root carried the idea of being bereft or empty, the state rather than the person.
items.cn: 这个词根带有「被夺走、空着」之意，强调状态而非人。

items.en: Widewe named a woman left without a husband, and the word carried legal weight in land claims.
items.cn: widewe 指失去丈夫的女性，这个词在土地归属中带有法律分量。

items.en: The form shifted to widwe and then widow, and the endings simplified.
items.cn: 词形先后变为 widwe 与 widow，词尾也随之简化。

items.en: Widower was coined by adding -er, completing a pair the older language had left unpaired.
items.cn: widower 是加 -er 造出来的，补齐了旧语言未曾成对的一面。

items.en: The word also entered printing and card games, where something stands alone at the top.
items.cn: 这个词也进入印刷与牌戏，用来指孤零零立在顶部的东西。

note.en: The first group gathers the family words that pair with widow, the second the words about loss and being left alone.
note.cn: 第一组收与 widow 成对的家族词，第二组收表示失去与独留的词。

entries.definition: A man whose wife has died, the male pair.
Having lost a husband or wife.
The state of being a widow.
An opening in a wall, one letter away.
A child whose parents have died.
Not married, but not because of death.
The adjective used for either sex.

normalIntro.en: Widow only differs from window by two letters, and the two are the usual source of confusion.
normalIntro.cn: widow 与 window 只差两个字母，两者是最常见的混淆源。

normal.en: A widow is a woman left, a widower is a man left, and the -er marks the man.
normal.cn: widow 是被留下的女人，widower 是被留下的男人，-er 标记男性。

normal.en: Window has an n, widow has none.
normal.cn: window 里有个 n，widow 里没有。

normal.en: The old root meant empty, which is why the word describes a state.
normal.cn: 古老的词根意为「空」，所以这个词描述的是状态。

normal.en: A war widow is a fixed collocation that appears in history books.
normal.cn: war widow 是历史书里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Printing calls a lone line a widow, alone at the top of a page.
normal.cn: 印刷业把页顶孤立的一行也叫 widow。

abstract.en: See one chair on a porch left empty.
abstract.cn: 看见门廊上留下的一把空椅子。

abstract.en: Feel a room that is still arranged for two.
abstract.cn: 感觉一间仍按两个人摆放的房间。

abstract.en: Hear a name spoken in the past tense.
abstract.cn: 听见一个用过去时被提起的名字。

examples.en: The widow runs the shop that her husband opened.
examples.cn: 这位寡妇经营着丈夫开的那家店。

examples.en: Many women were widowed during the long war.
examples.cn: 漫长的战争让许多女性成了寡妇。

examples.en: She has been a widow for nearly twenty years.
examples.cn: 她守寡将近二十年了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微多」——一个人微微多了些孤单，所以是寡妇。

root: 日耳曼语词根（空、被分开）→ 古英语 widewe → 中古英语 widow → 现代英语 widow；同族有 widower、widowed、widowhood。

sensesIntro.en: The word names a woman left by death, gives her a male pair, turns into the act of causing that state, and finally lends itself to a lone line on a page.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先命名因死亡而独留的女性，再配出男性一面，随后转成造成这种状态的动作，最后借给页面上孤立的一行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chair still standing where two once stood.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该两把椅子并排，却只剩一把。

branches.en: The woman branch: two chairs on the porch.
branches.cn: 女性分支：门廊上的两把椅子。

branches.en: The pair branch: law that spoke only of widows.
branches.cn: 成对分支：只说寡妇的法律。

branches.en: The verb branch: war widowing thousands.
branches.cn: 动词分支：战争使成千上万人丧偶。

branches.en: The printing branch: a lone line at the top.
branches.cn: 排版分支：页首孤立的一行。

branches.en: The games branch: one player without a partner.
branches.cn: 牌戏分支：没有搭档的那一位。

intro.en: Widow is a root word, and its small family is built with -er, -ed and -hood rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: widow 是词根词，它的小词族靠 -er、-ed、-hood 扩展，而不用前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Germanic root is distantly related to Latin vidua, which gives the English adjective vidual and the word viduity.
latinIntro.cn: 这个日耳曼语词根与拉丁语 vidua 有远亲关系，后者给出英语的 vidual 与 viduity。

items.meaning: a woman bereft of her husband
items.example: It works as noun and verb.
The possessive marks the older legal style.
items.exampleCN: 所有格标示旧式法律文体。

items.meaning: to lose a partner by death
items.example: The passive avoids naming the cause.

items.meaning: a historic phrase for a young widow
items.example: It names a social wrong of the past.
items.exampleCN: 它指认过去的一种社会弊端。

latinEntries.example: It is the direct Latin cousin of the Germanic word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是这个日耳曼词在拉丁语中的直接表亲。

latinEntries.example: It shows the old idea of emptiness.

definition_zh: 宽度；广度；宽度单位；宽容
definition_en: the measurement of something from one side to the other, and by extension the breadth of a range
core_image: 一把卷尺横拉过门框，尺上的数字正好停在九十几厘米
scene: 木匠把卷尺横着拉过门框，报出那一串数字，说这扇门就按这个宽度做。Measure the width of the window before you order the curtains.
sceneCN: 这里 width 是「宽度」（第 1 个义项：从一边到另一边量出的尺寸）；句意为订窗帘前先量出窗户的宽度。卷尺横拉过门框、数字停在那一格，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The measurement across
senses.definition: the distance a thing measures from one side to the other, the smaller of its two flat dimensions
senses.definitionCN: 物体从一边到另一边量出的距离，平面上两个尺寸中较小的那个
senses.example: Measure the width of the window before you order the curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 订窗帘前先量出窗户的宽度。
senses.why: The noun takes the adjective and turns the quality into a number you can write down.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把形容词的性质变成了能写下来的数字。

senses.title: A stated measure
senses.definition: used after a number to give the measurement, as in a width of three metres
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字之后给出尺寸，如 a width of three metres
senses.example: The table has a width of one metre and a half.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子宽一米半。
senses.why: The same word doubles as a unit, since English says a width of rather than a wide of.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词又充当量词，因为英语说 a width of，而不说 a wide of。

senses.title: Breadth of a range
senses.definition: the extent or variety included in something, especially knowledge or choice
senses.definitionCN: 某物所包含的程度或多样程度，尤指知识或选择
senses.example: The width of her reading surprised the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 她阅读面的广博让全班都很惊讶。
senses.why: A physical span became a mental one, and the measurement now counts kinds instead of metres.
senses.whyCN: 物理的跨度变成心智的跨度，度量的对象也从米变成种类。

senses.title: In textile and cut sizes
senses.definition: the measurement of cloth from selvedge to selvedge, as sold in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 商店出售布料时从一边布边到另一边的尺寸
senses.example: This cloth comes in two widths, ninety and one hundred and fifty centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 这种布有九十厘米和一百五十厘米两种幅宽。
senses.why: Shops need a fixed measure of cloth, so the general word became a trade term.
senses.whyCN: 商店需要固定的布料尺寸，于是普通词成了行业术语。

senses.title: In swimming pools and boats
senses.definition: used in the name of a pool or a boat class to state how wide it is
senses.definitionCN: 在泳池或船级名称中说明其宽度
senses.example: The pool has six lanes and a width of twenty metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个泳池有六条泳道，宽二十米。
senses.why: A standard measure became part of a name, and swimmers now speak of a twenty-metre width.
senses.whyCN: 一种标准度量进入了名称，游泳者于是说起「二十米宽」这样的说法。

intro.en: Width was formed in Middle English by adding the ending -th to wid, the same way length came from long and depth from deep.
intro.cn: width 是中古英语在 wid 上加词尾 -th 构成的，正如 length 来自 long、depth 来自 deep。

items.en: The adjective wid meant broad, and the ending -th already built nouns of measure such as lengu.
items.cn: 形容词 wid 表示宽阔，词尾 -th 早已能构成度量名词。

items.en: Widthe appeared as the noun of measurement, modelled on length and breadth.
items.cn: widthe 作为度量名词出现，仿照 length 与 breadth 的模式。

items.en: The spelling settled as width, with the short i of wide but a different vowel in careful speech.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 width，在某些口音里元音与 wide 略有不同。

items.en: Trade and tailoring gave it concrete uses such as the width of cloth.
items.cn: 商业与裁缝给了它具体用法，如布料的幅宽。

items.en: It also took an abstract life, so a person can have width of experience.
items.cn: 它也获得了抽象的生命，于是人可以有阅历之广度。

note.en: The first group gathers the other measurements of the same shape, the second the words that stand for breadth.
note.cn: 第一组收同一形状的其他度量名词，第二组收表示广度的词。

entries.definition: The measurement end to end, from long.
The measurement down, from deep.
The measurement across, from broad.
A preposition that merely looks close.
The same idea, often in a literary tone.
The full reach from one end to the other.
The extent covered by a set of things.

normalIntro.en: Width belongs to the th-family: length, depth, breadth, width, all nouns of measurement.
normalIntro.cn: width 属于 -th 家族：length、depth、breadth、width，都是度量名词。

normal.en: Long makes length and wide makes width, the -th is the measuring tool.
normal.cn: long 变 length，wide 变 width，那个 -th 就是量尺。

normal.en: Length runs along, width runs across, depth runs down.
normal.cn: length 竖着走，width 横着走，depth 往下走。

normal.en: A width of two metres never says a wide of two metres.
normal.cn: 要说 a width of two metres，不能说 a wide of。

normal.en: Width of reading counts kinds, not metres.
normal.cn: width of reading 数的是种类，不是米。

normal.en: Width and depth together describe a swimming pool.
normal.cn: width 与 depth 合起来描述一个泳池。

abstract.en: Feel a tape pulled tight across a door frame.
abstract.cn: 感觉卷尺绷紧横过门框。

abstract.en: See a number written down and the measure fixed for good.
abstract.cn: 看见数字被写下来，尺寸就此固定。

abstract.en: Hear cloth measured from edge to edge on a counter.
abstract.cn: 听柜台上的布从一边量到另一边。

examples.en: The width of the path is only one metre.
examples.cn: 这条小路的宽度只有一米。

examples.en: The skirt is available in three widths.
examples.cn: 这条裙子有三种宽度可选。

examples.en: What she lacks in width she makes up for in detail.
examples.cn: 她在广度上不足，便用细节来补。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微斯」——微微一点宽度也要量出来。

root: 古英语 wid（宽阔）+ 度量名词词尾 -th → 中古英语 widthe → 现代英语 width；同族有 wide、widen、widely、length、depth。

sensesIntro.en: The noun fixes the distance across, doubles as a unit, widens into mental breadth, and settles into the trades of cloth and pools.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词固定了横量的距离，兼作量词，扩展到心智的广度，并固定于布料与泳池行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape measure stretched across a door frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：一卷绷紧横过门框的卷尺。

branches.en: The curtain branch: measuring before ordering.
branches.cn: 窗帘分支：下订之前先量。

branches.en: The table branch: a width of one and a half metres.
branches.cn: 桌子分支：宽一米半。

branches.en: The reading branch: a class surprised by breadth.
branches.cn: 阅读分支：让全班惊讶的阅读广度。

branches.en: The trade branch: cloth in two widths.
branches.cn: 行业分支：两种幅宽的布料。

branches.en: The pool branch: six lanes, twenty metres wide.
branches.cn: 泳池分支：六条泳道，宽二十米。

intro.en: Width is a noun of quality and measure built with -th on an adjective, one of a small and ancient pattern.
intro.cn: width 是用 -th 加在形容词上构成的度量类抽象名词，属于一个小而古老的模式。

latinIntro.en: The base is native Germanic, so there is no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show the borrowed nouns of the same kind.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目展示同类的借入名词。

items.example: It forms width, length and depth.
A fixed frame after a number.
A common unit in sport and clothing.
items.exampleCN: 运动与服装中常见的度量。

latinEntries.example: It gives English latitude.
It gives English amplitude.

definition_zh: 妻子；夫人；（旧）妇女
definition_en: the woman a man or woman is married to, seen from the partner s side
core_image: 两只并排挂在门边的结婚戒指照片，框里两个人肩膀挨得很近
scene: 他指着厨房里那位系着围裙的人，说这就是他妻子，然后笑着去洗碗。His wife teaches at the school at the end of our street.
sceneCN: 这里 wife 是「妻子」（第 1 个义项：与之结婚的那位女性，从配偶一方来看）；句意为他妻子在我们街尾那所学校教书。门边并排挂着的合照，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The married partner
senses.definition: the woman to whom a person is married, spoken of from the other partner s side
senses.definitionCN: 一个人与之结婚的女性，从配偶另一方的角度来说
senses.example: His wife teaches at the school at the end of our street.
senses.exampleCN: 他妻子在我们街尾那所学校教书。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense, a role named from the viewpoint of the person married to her.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常意义，是从与她结婚之人的视角命名的一个角色。

senses.title: A woman in old use
senses.definition: in older English, any adult woman, without any link to marriage
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的英语中泛指成年女性，与婚姻无关
senses.example: In Middle English a wife could mean simply a woman of any rank.
senses.exampleCN: 在中古英语里，wife 可以单纯指任何身份的女性。
senses.why: The broad sense is the original one, and it survives today only inside fixed compounds.
senses.whyCN: 这个宽泛的意义才是最初的义项，今天只在固定复合词内部存活。

senses.title: In fixed pairs
senses.definition: used in paired phrases such as husband and wife or man and wife
senses.definitionCN: 用于 husband and wife、man and wife 这类成对说法
senses.example: They were pronounced man and wife before the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在全村人面前被宣布为夫妻。
senses.why: The wedding formula keeps the older style, and the pair sounds like one unit.
senses.whyCN: 婚礼套语保留了更古老的说法，这一对词听起来像一个整体。

senses.title: Inside compounds
senses.definition: used as a second element in words such as housewife and midwife
senses.definitionCN: 作为 housewife、midwife 等词的后项出现
senses.example: His mother had been a housewife for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他母亲做了三十年家庭主妇。
senses.why: Old compounds kept the broad sense of woman, which is why a midwife is not simply a married woman.
senses.whyCN: 古老的复合词保留了「女性」的宽泛意义，所以 midwife 并不只是已婚妇女。

senses.title: In respectful address
senses.definition: in older formal usage, a title for a married woman, often written before her family name
senses.definitionCN: 在旧式正式用法中，作为已婚女性的称谓，常写在姓氏之前
senses.example: The letter began with a greeting to the doctor and his wife.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信开头向医生和他的夫人问候。
senses.why: The title dropped out of most modern use, and the plain noun is now the neutral choice.
senses.whyCN: 这一称谓在现代多数用法中已消失，普通名词成为中性选择。

intro.en: Wife comes from Old English wif, which meant woman in general, not a married one; the narrowing to married partner came later.
intro.cn: wife 源自古英语 wif，本泛指女性而非已婚者，限定为配偶的意义是后来才出现的。

items.en: The root meant woman, and the related word for a male partner was separate.
items.cn: 这个词根意为女性，指男性配偶的词则另有一个。

items.en: Wif meant woman, and wifman and wermann paired a woman and a man as humans.
items.cn: wif 指女性，wifman 与 wermann 则以「人」为后项来指男女。

items.en: Wif narrowed towards married woman, while woman took over the general sense.
items.cn: wif 的词义收窄为已婚女性，泛指的意义由 woman 接手。

items.en: The plural wives kept the old f to v change, the only trace of the older grammar.
items.cn: 复数 wives 保留了 f 变 v 的变化，这是旧语法的唯一痕迹。

items.en: Compounds such as housewife and midwife still carry the older sense of woman.
items.cn: housewife 与 midwife 这类复合词仍带着旧有的「女性」之义。

note.en: The first group gathers the marriage and family words that look close, the second the words for a partner in general.
note.cn: 第一组收形近的婚姻与家庭词，第二组收泛指伴侣的词。

entries.definition: The male partner in the same relationship.
The plural, with f turned to v.
The state of being alive, one letter apart.
A cutting tool, the same f sound.
A partner in marriage, of either sex.
The person one lives with or shares life with.
A woman on her wedding day.

normalIntro.en: Wife has only one irregular point, the plural wives, and one surprising fact, that it once meant woman.
normalIntro.cn: wife 只有一个不规则点，即复数 wives，还有一个意外事实：它原本指「女性」。

normal.en: Wife turns to wives, and so do knife and life.
normal.cn: wife 变 wives，knife 和 life 也一样。

normal.en: Husband and wife is a fixed pair that reads like one word.
normal.cn: husband and wife 是固定一对，读起来像一个词。

normal.en: A midwife helps at births because the old word meant a woman.
normal.cn: midwife 负责接生，因为旧义就是「女性」。

normal.en: The -fe ending is the only sign of the old grammar left.
normal.cn: 这个 -fe 词尾是旧语法留下的唯一迹象。

normal.en: Remember it as a role seen from the partner s side.
normal.cn: 把它记作从配偶那一侧看到的角色。

abstract.en: See two rings hanging side by side by a door.
abstract.cn: 看见两枚戒指并排挂在门边。

abstract.en: Hear a name introduced with one word in front of it.
abstract.cn: 听一个名字前面只加了一个词就被介绍出来。

abstract.en: Feel a shoulder close to another shoulder in an old photo.
abstract.cn: 感觉老照片里一个肩膀紧挨着另一个肩膀。

examples.en: He and his wife have lived here for forty years.
examples.cn: 他和妻子在这里住了四十年。

examples.en: The two of them were man and wife by the end of the day.
examples.cn: 一天结束的时候，他们俩成了夫妻。

examples.en: The old house belonged to the doctor and his wife.
examples.cn: 那所老房子属于医生和他夫人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怀福」——怀里揣着福气的人，就是妻子。

root: 日耳曼语词根（女性）→ 古英语 wif（女人）→ 中古英语 wif（妻子）→ 现代英语 wife；同族有 wives、housewife、midwife。

sensesIntro.en: The word began as woman, narrowed to the married partner, settled in wedding formulas, lived on inside compounds, and faded as a title of address.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词原本指女性，收窄为配偶，固定在婚礼套语里，存活于复合词内部，最后作为称谓逐渐淡出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings hanging side by side by the same door.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一扇门边并排挂着的两枚戒指。

branches.en: The everyday branch: a teacher at the end of the street.
branches.cn: 日常分支：街尾教书的妻子。

branches.en: The old branch: any woman of any rank.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：任何身份的女性。

branches.en: The wedding branch: pronounced man and wife.
branches.cn: 婚礼分支：被宣布为夫妻。

branches.en: The compound branch: thirty years as a housewife.
branches.cn: 复合词分支：三十年家庭主妇。

branches.en: The title branch: a letter to the doctor and his wife.
branches.cn: 称谓分支：写给医生夫妇的信。

intro.en: Wife is a root noun whose plural is irregular, and it survives inside old compounds where the second place was once open to any word for woman.
intro.cn: wife 是复数不规则的词根名词，它在古老的复合词中仍然存活，那些复合词的后项原本可换成任何表示女性的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below give the borrowed words that translate it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目给出用来翻译它的借入词。

items.example: It gives midwife, a woman who helps at birth.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 midwife，即接生的女性。

items.example: The wedding formula of the old style.
The pair reads as one unit.
items.exampleCN: 这一对读来像一个整体。

latinEntries.example: It gives the adjective uxorious.
It shows the older broad sense side by side.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它与更宽泛的旧义并立。

definition_zh: 野生的；荒野的；狂热的；失控的；荒凉的
definition_en: living or growing freely in nature without people, and figuratively uncontrolled, violent or very enthusiastic
core_image: 一片没有篱笆的草坡，风一过草就朝同一个方向倒，中间有一条窄窄的兽径
scene: 山坡上没有篱笆、没有人修的路，只有一条被野兽踩出来的窄径，草随风倒向一边。Wild horses still run on this island in summer.
sceneCN: 这里 wild 是「野生的」（第 1 个义项：在自然中自由生长或生活、未经人驯养）；句意为夏天这个岛上仍有野马奔跑。没有篱笆的草坡与那条兽径，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 野生的；无人居住的；狂热的；失控的

senses.title: Living free in nature
senses.definition: used of plants and animals that grow or live without being kept or planted by people
senses.definitionCN: 形容未被人饲养或栽种的动植物
senses.example: Wild horses still run on this island in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天这个岛上仍有野马奔跑。
senses.why: The oldest sense is untamed, which is the state of a creature that no one owns or feeds.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是未被驯服，即没有任何人拥有或喂养的状态。

senses.title: Land without people
senses.definition: used of country that is empty, rough and not farmed or built on
senses.definitionCN: 形容空旷、崎岖、未被耕种或建起的土地
senses.example: Beyond the village there are miles of wild hills.
senses.exampleCN: 村子外面是连绵数里的荒山。
senses.why: An untamed creature needs untamed land, so the word covers the ground as well as its inhabitants.
senses.whyCN: 未经驯服的动物需要未经驯服的土地，于是这个词也覆盖了地面。

senses.title: Out of control
senses.definition: used of behaviour, weather or imagination that runs without restraint
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为、天气或想象失去约束地奔流
senses.example: The crowd went wild when the winning goal went in.
senses.exampleCN: 制胜球进门时，人群发狂了。
senses.why: A wild horse cannot be led, and human feeling that cannot be led takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 野马牵不动，而牵不动的人的情绪也用同一个词。

senses.title: Very keen on something
senses.definition: in informal use, extremely enthusiastic about a person or activity
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示对某人或某事极度热衷
senses.example: The children are wild about the new cartoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们对这部新动画片着迷得不行。
senses.why: Enthusiasm without restraint is another way of being untamed, so the word softened into liking.
senses.whyCN: 不知节制的热情也是未驯服的一种，于是这个词软化成喜欢。

senses.title: Rough and inaccurate
senses.definition: used of a guess or a claim that is made without care or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容猜测或断言轻率、没有依据
senses.example: It was only a wild guess, but it turned out right.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是个胡猜，结果竟然猜对了。
senses.why: An arrow shot without aim flies wild, and a guess without aim takes the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 不经瞄准射出的箭会乱飞，不经瞄准的猜测也用这个形容词。

intro.en: Wild comes from Old English wilde, meaning untamed and living in the forest, from a Germanic word for the uncontrolled.
intro.cn: wild 源自古英语 wilde，意为未被驯服、生活在林野之中，其日耳曼语源头与「无约束」有关。

items.en: The root described what was not under human hand, whether a beast or a wood.
items.cn: 这个词根描述不受人手掌控之物，无论野兽还是林子。

items.en: Wilde meant untamed and also described empty, uncultivated land.
items.cn: wilde 表示未被驯服，也描述空旷未耕的土地。

items.en: The word moved from the forest to people, so a wild mood was one without restraint.
items.cn: 这个词从林子移向人，于是 wild mood 指不受约束的情绪。

items.en: Sports writing made go wild the phrase for a crowd losing control.
items.cn: 体育写作让 go wild 成为形容人群失控的说法。

items.en: Casual speech softened it into enthusiasm, as in wild about a band.
items.cn: 口语把它软化为热情，如 wild about a band。

note.en: The first group gathers the closely related wild- words, the second the words for untamed things and land.
note.cn: 第一组收密切相关的 wild- 词族，第二组收表示未驯服之物与土地的词。

entries.definition: Animals and plants living free.
In an uncontrolled way, or very much.
Large land left untamed.
Broad, differing by one sound.
Not made tame or obedient.
Violent and dangerous in attack.
Unprocessed, rough and direct.

normalIntro.en: Wild is a short word with a lot of force, so keep the untamed creature and let the other senses grow from it.
normalIntro.cn: wild 很短却很有力，记住那只未驯服的野兽，其他义项都从它长出来。

normal.en: Wild is the opposite of tame, and a tame horse can be led.
normal.cn: wild 与 tame 相对，而驯服的马是能牵走的。

normal.en: Go wild, run wild, wild guess: all have no rein.
normal.cn: go wild、run wild、wild guess：都没有缰绳。

normal.en: Wild about means keen, the same no-rein energy turned to liking.
normal.cn: wild about 表示热衷，是同一股无缰的劲头变成了喜欢。

normal.en: Wildlife and wilderness both start from this one word.
normal.cn: wildlife 与 wilderness 都从这个词出发。

normal.en: Wild differs from wide only in the final sound.
normal.cn: wild 与 wide 只差最后一个音。

abstract.en: Feel grass bend all the way over in one wind.
abstract.cn: 感觉草被一阵风整个压弯。

abstract.en: See a narrow track made by animals, not people.
abstract.cn: 看见一条由动物而非人踩出的小径。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd roaring louder than the whistle.
abstract.cn: 听见人群的吼声比哨声还响。

examples.en: Wild flowers line the path every spring.
examples.cn: 每年春天小路两边都开满野花。

examples.en: The crowd went wild when the singer appeared.
examples.cn: 歌手出现时人群沸腾了。

examples.en: Beyond the wall the land turns wild and rocky.
examples.cn: 墙那边土地变得荒凉多石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪的」——长歪了没人管，就变成野生的了。

root: 日耳曼语词根（不受掌控）→ 古英语 wilde（未驯服、荒芜）→ 中古英语 wild → 现代英语 wild；同族有 wildly、wilderness、wildlife。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a creature no one owns, spreads to land with no people, jumps to feeling without a rein, softens into keen liking, and ends with a guess that has no aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从无人拥有的生物出发，扩展到无人的土地，跳到没有缰绳的情绪，软化为热衷，最后落在没有瞄准的猜测上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fenceless slope with one narrow track worn by animals.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有篱笆的草坡，只有一条兽径。

branches.en: The horses branch: wild horses on the island.
branches.cn: 野马分支：岛上的野马。

branches.en: The hills branch: miles of rough empty land.
branches.cn: 山野分支：连绵数里的荒山。

branches.en: The crowd branch: roaring at the winning goal.
branches.cn: 人群分支：制胜球时的怒吼。

branches.en: The fan branch: children and a new cartoon.
branches.cn: 粉丝分支：孩子与新动画。

branches.en: The guess branch: right by accident.
branches.cn: 猜测分支：碰巧猜对。

intro.en: Wild is a free adjective that builds the -ly adverb, the -ness noun and the older noun wilderness, and it heads compounds such as wildlife.
intro.cn: wild 是自由使用的形容词，可派生 -ly 副词、-ness 名词与较古老的 wilderness，还作为前项构成 wildlife 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show the borrowed words for untamed nature.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目展示表示未经驯服之自然的借入词。

items.example: It works as adjective, noun and adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它可作形容词、名词与副词。

items.example: It forms wildly, also meaning very.
The crowd picture in two words.
items.exampleCN: 两个词画出人群的画面。

items.example: It suits children and gardens alike.
items.exampleCN: 它既适合孩子也适合园子。

items.example: The adjective turned noun keeps the land.
items.exampleCN: 形容词转名词后保留了土地之意。

latinEntries.example: It gives English feral.
It gives English sylvan.

definition_zh: 狂野地；失控地；极度地；胡乱地
definition_en: in an uncontrolled manner, and in informal use to a very great degree
core_image: 一匹没上缰绳的马，在空地上左右乱冲，方向完全不由人
scene: 那匹马突然甩开缰绳，在空地上左右乱冲，谁都拉不住。The crowd cheered wildly as the team came out.
sceneCN: 这里 wildly 是「狂野地、失控地」（第 1 个义项：以无法控制的方式）；句意为人群在球队出场时狂热欢呼。甩开缰绳乱冲的马，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 狂野地；失控地；极度地；胡乱地

senses.title: Without control
senses.definition: in a way that shows no restraint or control
senses.definitionCN: 以毫无约束或控制的方式
senses.example: The crowd cheered wildly as the team came out.
senses.exampleCN: 球队出场时，人群狂热欢呼。
senses.why: The adverb simply reports the untamed quality as the manner of a verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是把「未驯服」的性质作为动作的方式报告出来。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: in informal use, used before adjectives to mean extremely
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在形容词前，表示极度
senses.example: The first attempt was wildly successful.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次尝试大获成功。
senses.why: A wild horse goes much further than a tame one, so the word became a strong intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 野马比驯马跑得远得多，于是这个词成了强力的强调词。

senses.title: With great variation
senses.definition: used of numbers or opinions that differ by a very large amount
senses.definitionCN: 形容数字或意见相差极大
senses.example: Estimates of the cost vary wildly.
senses.exampleCN: 对成本的估计差别极大。
senses.why: The adverb measures how far apart things are, and the distance is stretched wide.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词度量事物相距多远，而这段距离被拉得很宽。

senses.title: Without aim
senses.definition: used of shooting, swinging or guessing done with no aim
senses.definitionCN: 形容射击、挥打或猜测没有瞄准
senses.example: He swung wildly at the ball and missed completely.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝球胡乱一挥，完全打空。
senses.why: A shot with no aim flies wild, and the adverb keeps that picture of an arrow off course.
senses.whyCN: 没瞄准的一击会乱飞，而副词保留了那支偏离轨道的箭。

intro.en: Wildly is wild plus -ly, and it grew from describing animals to describing voices, numbers and praise.
intro.cn: wildly 是 wild 加 -ly，其用法从描述兽类扩展到声音、数字与称赞。

items.en: Wilde described untamed creatures and empty land, and did not yet need an adverb form.
items.cn: wilde 描述未驯服的兽与空旷的土地，当时还不需要副词形式。

items.en: Wildliche appears for acting in a wild manner, first of movement and weather.
items.cn: 中古英语的 wildliche 表示以狂野的方式行动，最初用于动作与天气。

items.en: The spelling became wildly, and it described how people laughed, ran and shouted.
items.cn: 拼写变为 wildly，用来描述人如何大笑、奔跑与呼喊。

items.en: Before adjectives it became an informal intensifier, as in wildly popular.
items.cn: 放在形容词前，它成为口语中的强调成分，如 wildly popular。

items.en: It also came to measure disagreement, as in estimates that vary wildly.
items.cn: 它还用来形容意见分歧，如 vary wildly 的估计。

note.en: The first group gathers other wild- words, the second the adverbs that mean very much or with no control.
note.cn: 第一组收其他 wild- 词族成员，第二组收表示「极度」「失控」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb.
The noun of being wild.
The noun for untamed land.
Gladly, sharing a similar ending shape.
In a fast, anxious, out-of-control way.
To a very great degree, the neutral choice.
With violent force or strong feeling.

normalIntro.en: Wildly takes wild and adds the plain -ly, so its two jobs are manner and degree.
normalIntro.cn: wildly 就是 wild 加普通 -ly，所以它做两件事：方式与程度。

normal.en: Wild gives the horse, ly turns it into how the horse moves.
normal.cn: wild 给出那匹马，ly 把它变成马奔跑的方式。

normal.en: Wildly successful is the informal intensifier, stronger than very.
normal.cn: wildly successful 是口语强调，比 very 更强。

normal.en: Vary wildly measures a gap, not a gesture.
normal.cn: vary wildly 量的是差距，不是动作。

normal.en: Cheer wildly needs a crowd and a finished race.
normal.cn: cheer wildly 需要一群人，还需要一场比完的赛。

normal.en: Swing wildly means the bat went where the ball was not.
normal.cn: swing wildly 说明拍子挥到了球不在的地方。

abstract.en: See a horse loose at full speed across an empty field.
abstract.cn: 看见一匹脱缰之马在空地上全速乱冲。

abstract.en: Hear a cheer that goes on after the whistle.
abstract.cn: 听见哨声之后仍在继续的欢呼。

abstract.en: Feel a guess fly off the page and miss.
abstract.cn: 感觉一个猜测飞出纸面，落了个空。

examples.en: The dog ran wildly round the garden.
examples.cn: 那只狗在花园里狂乱地跑。

examples.en: The book was wildly popular among students.
examples.cn: 这本书在学生中极受欢迎。

examples.en: Prices here have fluctuated wildly this year.
examples.cn: 今年这里的价格剧烈波动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪的理」——歪道理讲得又急又乱，狂野地往外冒。

root: 古英语 wilde（未驯服）+ 副词词尾 -ly → 中古英语 wildliche → 现代英语 wildly；同族有 wild、wildness、wilderness。

sensesIntro.en: The word describes a way of moving without control, then a very high degree, then a wide difference, and finally a swing with no aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先描述失控的动作方式，再表示很高的程度，然后是很大的差别，最后是没有瞄准的一挥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horse loose with the reins dragging.
core.cn: 核心意象：一匹脱缰的马，缰绳拖在地上。

branches.en: The cheer branch: a crowd past the whistle.
branches.cn: 欢呼分支：哨声已过仍在喊的人群。

branches.en: The success branch: a first try that worked.
branches.cn: 成功分支：第一次就成的尝试。

branches.en: The estimate branch: prices far apart.
branches.cn: 估计分支：相差极大的价格。

branches.en: The swing branch: missing the ball completely.
branches.cn: 挥击分支：完全打空。

branches.en: The intensity branch: manner and degree in one word.
branches.cn: 强度分支：一词兼顾方式与程度。

intro.en: Wildly is a plain -ly adverb, and the suffix does nothing more than turn the untamed adjective into a description of how something happens.
intro.cn: wildly 是普通的 -ly 副词，后缀只是把「未驯服」的形容词变成「如何发生」的描述。

latinIntro.en: The base is native Germanic, so there is no Latin source; the Latin entries below give the borrowed adverbs of the same force.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出同等力度的借入副词。

latinEntries.example: It comes from ferus, wild.
It lies behind vehemence.

definition_zh: 将；会；愿意；意志；遗嘱
definition_en: the word that marks the future or a decision, and the noun for the power to choose, or for a document about property after death
core_image: 一个人伸手推开一扇沉重的门，手已经按在门上，还没推
scene: 他站在门口，手按在门板上停了一下，然后说他会去把这件事办完。I will call you as soon as the meeting ends.
sceneCN: 这里 will 是「将、会」（第 1 个义项：表示将来或决定）；句意为会议一结束我就给你打电话。那只已经按在门上、还没推开的手，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Marking the future
senses.definition: used with another verb to speak about the future or about what is expected
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个动词连用，谈论将来或预期会发生的事
senses.example: I will call you as soon as the meeting ends.
senses.exampleCN: 会议一结束我就给你打电话。
senses.why: The future use grew out of the older sense of wanting, since what one wants tends to happen next.
senses.whyCN: 将来义从旧的「想要」义长出来，因为人想要的往往是接下来会发生的事。

senses.title: Expressing a decision or promise
senses.definition: used to show a choice just made, a promise or a refusal
senses.definitionCN: 表示刚做出的选择、承诺或拒绝
senses.example: I will not lend him the car again.
senses.exampleCN: 我再也不把车借给他了。
senses.why: Here the word is doing what it did first, putting a wish into a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词做的是它最早的工作：把一个意愿放进句子。

senses.title: The power to choose
senses.definition: the mental power by which a person decides and keeps to a choice
senses.definitionCN: 一个人作出决定并坚持下去的心理力量
senses.example: It took great will to finish the climb in that wind.
senses.exampleCN: 在那样的风里爬完全程需要极大的意志。
senses.why: The noun names the faculty behind every use of the modal, the inner hand on the door.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名了每一个情态用法背后的能力，也就是那只按在门上的手。

senses.title: A document after death
senses.definition: a legal paper saying who should receive a person s property after death
senses.definitionCN: 一份法律文件，说明一个人去世后财产归谁
senses.example: She made a will and left the house to her niece.
senses.exampleCN: 她立了遗嘱，把房子留给侄女。
senses.why: The document states a person s last wishes, so the word for wanting became the word for the paper.
senses.whyCN: 这份文件陈述一个人最后的意思，于是表示「意愿」的词成了文件之名。

senses.title: To make something happen by wanting
senses.definition: in a somewhat formal use, to bring something about by determination, or to leave property by a will
senses.definitionCN: 在稍正式用法中，指凭决心促成某事，或指按遗嘱留下财产
senses.example: He willed himself to stay calm in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他在大厅里强使自己保持镇定。
senses.why: The noun turned back into a verb, so a person can now will a result or will a house to a friend.
senses.whyCN: 名词又转回动词，于是人可以用意志促成结果，或把房子遗赠给朋友。

intro.en: Will comes from Old English willan, to wish, and the same word served both as noun and as verb from the beginning.
intro.cn: will 源自古英语 willan（希望），从一开始就兼作名词与动词。

items.en: The root meant to wish or to want, and the noun named the wishing itself.
items.cn: 这个词根表示希望、想要，名词则命名这个「希望」本身。

items.en: Willan was the verb of wishing, and willa the noun for a wish or a purpose.
items.cn: willan 是表示希望的动词，willa 是表示愿望或目的的名词。

items.en: The word gained the future use, at first for intention, then for plain prediction.
items.cn: 这个词获得了将来用法，先表示意图，后表示单纯的预测。

items.en: The contraction won’t came from wol not and settled as the negative form.
items.cn: 缩写 won’t 来自 wol not，最终固定为否定形式。

items.en: The legal sense of a will for property dates from the same period and is now the main noun use.
items.cn: 表示财产文件的法律义同出一时代，如今是该名词的主要用法。

note.en: The first group gathers the other ways English marks the future or willingness, the second the nouns for purpose and choice.
note.cn: 第一组收英语中其他表示将来或意愿的形式，第二组收表示目的与选择的词。

entries.definition: The past of will, also a polite form.
Ready to do something, an adjective.
A short form used in speech, close in shape.
In a good way, differing by one letter.
The older future word, now formal or legal.
To want something that may not happen.
What a person means to do.

normalIntro.en: Will is one short word doing three jobs, so remember the picture of the hand on the door and let grammar follow.
normalIntro.cn: will 一个短词担三份工，记住那只按在门上的手，语法自然跟上。

normal.en: Will began as wanting, so willing and wish sit in the same family.
normal.cn: will 原本是「想要」，所以 willing 与 wish 同属一家。

normal.en: I will is both a promise and a future, since a promise is a small future.
normal.cn: I will 既是承诺也是将来，因为承诺就是一个小小的将来。

normal.en: Won’t looks nothing like will, and that odd shape makes it easy to recall.
normal.cn: won’t 看起来和 will 毫无关系，这种奇特形状反而容易记。

normal.en: Free will and will power both count the inner strength.
normal.cn: free will 与 will power 都在数内心的力量。

normal.en: A will for property is simply a person s last wish written down.
normal.cn: 关于财产的 will 就是把一个人最后的心愿写下来。

abstract.en: See a hand resting on a heavy door before the push.
abstract.cn: 看见一只手在推之前先按在沉重的门上。

abstract.en: Hear a promise said with the chin lifted.
abstract.cn: 听见一个抬着下巴说出的承诺。

abstract.en: Feel the effort of not turning back halfway.
abstract.cn: 感觉半路上忍住不回头的那股劲。

examples.en: I will meet you at the station at six.
examples.cn: 我六点在车站接你。

examples.en: She has a strong will and never gives up easily.
examples.cn: 她意志坚强，从不轻易放弃。

examples.en: He left the farm to his son in his will.
examples.cn: 他在遗嘱里把农场留给了儿子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为尔」——为了你才愿意去做，这就是意志与心愿。

root: 日耳曼语词根（希望、想要）→ 古英语 willan（希望）→ 中古英语 will → 现代英语 will；同族有 would、willing、willingly、willingness。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as wanting, serves to mark what will happen, names the power of choice, becomes the paper of last wishes, and finally returns as a verb of determination.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「想要」开始，用来标记将发生之事，命名选择的力量，变成写最后心愿的纸，最后作为表决心的动词回来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a heavy door, not yet pushing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在沉重的门上，还没推开。

branches.en: The future branch: I will call after the meeting.
branches.cn: 将来分支：会后我给你打电话。

branches.en: The refusal branch: I will not lend the car.
branches.cn: 拒绝分支：不再借车。

branches.en: The strength branch: finishing a climb in wind.
branches.cn: 力量分支：顶着风爬完全程。

branches.en: The document branch: the house left to a niece.
branches.cn: 文件分支：房子留给侄女。

branches.en: The effort branch: willing oneself to stay calm.
branches.cn: 努力分支：强使自己保持镇定。

intro.en: Will is a root word with no affixes, and its family grows by -ing forms and by the irregular past would.
intro.cn: will 是不带词缀的词根词，其词族靠 -ing 形式与不规则的过去式 would 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin source; the Latin entries below show the borrowed words about will and testaments.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目展示关于意愿与遗嘱的借入词。

items.exampleCN: 它可作情态动词、名词与动词。

items.example: An irregular shape from wol not.
items.exampleCN: 由 wol not 而来的不规则形式。

items.example: The noun in a small frame.

It gives the English testament and testamentary.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它给出英语的 testament 与 testamentary。
